A summer of change off the pitch for Aston Villa was followed by one of the worst opening 45 minutes of a season in Premier League history as Unai Emery’s side collapsed at Brighton and went into half-time 4-0 down

Last season’s Europa League winners went into the new campaign having lost four of the players that started their 3-0 win over Freiburg in May. Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa’s exits could also soon be followed by two more first-team stars in Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez, who were both left out of Villa’s matchday squad at Brighton.

A new-look Villa went behind inside eight minutes in calamitous fashion as Victor Lindelof bundled into his own net before Brighton’s Maxim De Cuyper doubled their advantage. Jack Hinshelwood then scored twice in two minutes before Villa’s Joao Gomes, a £38m signing from Wolves, was sent off on his first Premier League appearance for his new club.

open image in gallery Unai Emery speaks to Joao Gomes after his red card ( Getty )

Hinshelwood’s first goal was followed by another straight from kick-off. Gomes was caught in possession on the edge of his own box before Hinshelwood finished into an empty net for his second - just 80 seconds after his first.

It then went from bad to worse for debutant Gomes, who was earlier booked for waving an imaginary yellow card towards Pascal Gross, as he received a straight red card for kicking out at Georginio Rutter.

According to Opta, Gomes became just the second Premier League player to be sent off in the first half of his first appearance for the club, after QPR's Samba Diakite in 2012, while Brighton became just the third team to lead by four goals at half-time on the opening weekend in Premier League history.

There were empty seats in the Villa away end before half-time amid a hugely uncertain period for the Europa League winners, although the fans who remained continued to chant Emery’s name.

Brighton did not add any more goals in the second half, although Fabian Hurzeler did take the opportunity to rest some players ahead of Thursday’s Conference League play-off second leg against Tromso.

open image in gallery There were empty seats in the Villa end before half time ( Getty )

open image in gallery Villa fans saw their team fall apart in the first half ( Getty )

Villa have recouped huge fees for their departing stars, receiving a record £117m for Rogers from Chelsea, £51m for England defender Konsa and £35m for Tielemans, but the uncertainty off the field is undoubtedly a concern.

Villa have broken their transfer record to sign Johan Manzambi, who was unavailable due to injury, while Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki appears to be the replacement for Martinez but was only ready to be named on the bench.

Alejandro Garnacho and Aaron Wan-Bissaka have arrived on loan and Matteo Ruggeri has been signed as Emery attempts to rebuild his side. They have also been linked with a move for Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson.

“I’m very excited, I think we have had an intelligent market,” Emery said on Friday. “We know where we are and we know what we want to do again for the next year. This is the priority and this is the motivation I have.”

Villa striker Watkins is wanted by Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, and his omission from the travelling squad to the south coast will only heighten speculation that the England international is set to join the exodus.

Manager Emery provided a bizarre response when asked if this omission signalled the end for Watkins’ time at Villa, taking a lengthy pause before replying: "Silence." Emery previously said in a press conference that he wants to keep Watkins but has already confirmed that bids have been made for the 30-year-old.

Next up for Villa is a home match against Premier League champions Arsenal on Monday.

Lando Norris breathed further life into his F1 title defence with a brilliant Dutch Grand Prix victory as Max Verstappen’s final home race ended with him walking away from a huge opening-lap crash.

The world champion made it back-to-back wins with a brilliant drive, allowing him to execute a superb McLaren strategy to reel in title leader Kimi Antonelli.

Norris, whose victory last time out in Budapest was the first of a difficult title defence, admitted he has not lost hope of retaining his crown despite a hefty deficit – this win in Zandvoort still leaving him 83 points adrift.

But the manner of his win will raise belief, Norris outgunning Mercedes duo Antonelli and George Russell in qualifying and the race in his upgraded McLaren.

Russell boosted his title hopes by clinching sprint race victory on Saturday, but he was asked to allow his teammate and championship rival Antonelli through in the closing stages.

That allowed Antonelli to claim second while Russell then had to fend off Lewis Hamilton to secure third – with the British pair now level and 59 points adrift of Antonelli. Verstappen’s high-speed crash on lap one brought desperate disappointment to his adoring home fans at Zandvoort.

The four-time world champion is not in race-winning contention this season, but the huge crowds are almost exclusively here for him, his name chanted at every opportunity.

Seeing him step out of the wreckage of his Red Bull, which careered into the barriers at turn one, was not the ending they hoped to see in the final race at the circuit he helped return to the Formula One calendar.

Charles Leclerc was fifth for Ferrari ahead of McLaren’s Oscar Piastri.

open image in gallery Red Bull’s Max Verstappen crashed out of the race on the opening lap ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Norris won from pole after an action-packed grand prix ( PA )

The previous five races at Zandvoort have been won from pole position, claimed by Norris after a brilliant qualifying display on Saturday.

Heavy rain swept in 45 minutes before lights out in the seaside town, but the track was dry enough at lights out for the entire field to start on slick tyres.

Norris started well but Russell got an awful getaway from second, sliding out of his grid box, which allowed Antonelli to breeze past.

Top 10 – Dutch Grand Prix 1. Lando Norris (McLaren) 2. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) 3. George Russell (Mercedes) 4. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) 5. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) 6. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) 7. Liam Lawson (Red Bull) 8. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi) 9. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin) 10. Pierre Gasly (Alpine)

Verstappen was engaged in an elbows-out tussle with team-mate for the weekend Liam Lawson during the opening exchanges but, having won that duel, his race soon came to a shuddering halt.

The four-time world champion, revered in these parts, appeared to dip a wheel onto the kerb on the inside of the 18-degree banked final bend before sliding across the track and thundering into the barriers.

His Red Bull wreckage bounced back across the track ahead of Pierre Gasly and Arvid Lindblad, while his left-rear tyre flew off and went trundling away.

Verstappen confirmed he was ok as the race was red-flagged, before saying: “Yeah that’s it. Ah, I’m sorry guys.”

Almost simultaneously, Gabriel Bortoleto spun, his tyres throwing up a cloud of smoke through which teammate Nico Hulkenberg drove – narrowly avoiding a huge collision.

A delay of 30 minutes followed before Antonelli and Norris went wheel-to-wheel at turn one, Antonelli forcing his way past the reigning world champion.

Russell was then caught out by a brave move from McLaren’s Piastri as the Australian dived up the inside to claim third.

Ferrari were engaged in a tense radio battle as Hamilton urged them to let him past Leclerc, with the team telling the Monegasque to pit.

He was unhappy with that plan, ultimately pitting a lap later. “Great way of wasting time guys, good job,” Hamilton sarcastically said.

open image in gallery Lewis Hamilton finished fourth ( PA )

Norris made his final stop seven laps later than Antonelli in a bid to reel in the leader, and it was a perfect strategy call as he charged after the Italian, ultimately blasting past round the outside of turn one on lap 54.

“I made it tough for myself today but a good race,” said Norris. “Well fought. Probably one of my better wins. We had to fight for it.

“The pace was very strong and I managed things incredibly well today. Over the moon, very happy and nice to win the final race here in Zandvoort.”

Antonelli, Hamilton and Leclerc all then chose to pit under the virtual safety car, lifting Russell to second but with those behind on fresher rubber.

He was soon a man under fire, with Antonelli the first on his gearbox and Mercedes were quick to intervene, asking Russell to make way for his championship rival.

Russell cordially obliged, albeit with some protest, as he knew he was then at risk from Hamilton. But Russell held firm – crucially for his title hopes.

For Antonelli, he walks away having extended his championship lead, but Norris has moved up to fourth and is putting himself back in the title conversation.

Meghan Markle may not be appearing in the third season of Guy Ritchie’s The Gentlemen after all.

This week, reports that the Duchess of Sussex, 45, was considering a return to acting in the Netflix series sparked waves of backlash in the U.K.

Now, former Vanity Fair and New York Magazine editor-in-chief Tina Brown claims the decision to cast Meghan in the drama has been reversed.

“I learned this morning that the casting of Meghan Markle in season 3 of Guy Ritchie’s Netflix series The Gentlemen has been withdrawn,” Brown — who is the author of two books about the Royal Family — wrote on her Substack Saturday.

“The backlash in the UK was so intense, it became untenable to go forward,” she added.

The Independent has reached out to Netflix, Meghan and Ritchie for comment.

open image in gallery Meghan Markle’s acting comeback has reportedly been derailed ( AFP/Getty )

According to Variety, Meghan was in discussions to join the third installment of the series, starring Theo James and Kaya Scodelario, which films in the U.K.

The show is a spin-off of Guy Ritchie’s popular 2019 crime comedy movie of the same name, which starred Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam and Colin Farrell.

The third season of the show has not been officially greenlit. Season two premieres September 3.

The duke and duchess revealed earlier this month that they would be moving from California back to the U.K. with their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, who are both enrolled in British schools, six years after they came to the U.S.

open image in gallery Guy Ritchie’s ‘The Gentlemen’ films in the UK, where Harry and Meghan are returning after six years in the US ( Christopher Rafael/Netflix )

Brown reported that the upcoming move across the pond was partly inspired by Meghan’s potential gig in The Gentlemen.

It would have been her first acting role since she quit performing in 2017, when she got engaged to Prince Harry.

However, she recently appeared on screen in a cameo as herself in the upcoming Amazon MGM comedy Close Personal Friends, which stars Lily Collins and Brie Larson.

It marked Meghan’s first performance in nearly a decade after she rose to fame for her role as Rachel Zane in seven seasons of the legal drama Suits. She also appeared in films including Horrible Bosses, A Lot Like Love and Random Encounters.

Powerful leaders in the entertainment industry have spoken out to say that directors and producers will undoubtedly be eager to meet with Meghan if she has officially decided to resume her acting career.

For once, things will be moving quickly in the nation's capital as Washington hosts an IndyCar race through its streets.

President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump made the short drive Sunday afternoon to the course of the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, where cars will whip through the city’s downtown, including a stretch along Pennsylvania Avenue not too far from the White House.

“Their beautiful cars are going to make freedom roar. This will be a freedom that’s roaring like never before,” Trump said at the White House earlier this month as he promoted the event.

Before the race, Trump and his wife led a traditional prerace kickoff in his presidential limo. They could be seen waving through the windows, with a Marine Corps band playing “Stars and Stripes Forever" as the vehicles in the motorcade started rolling.

Air Force One, escorted by four fighter jets, flew overhead at the same time.

“I’m going to make a little circle in a nice, secure car, slightly slower than the ones we’re going to witness, but we’re going to have fun," Trump said in an interview on Fox shortly before the ride.

The open-wheel race, with cars whizzing past Washington’s monuments at speeds approaching 200 mph, is the latest of Trump’s celebrations this year to mark America’s 250th birthday.

Trump’s other events to mark the semiquincentennial of the Declaration of Independence’s signing have included a UFC fight on the White House lawn, military aircraft flyovers, a massive July Fourth fireworks show on the National Mall and a Great American State Fair that the president headlined after scores of ’90s-era musical acts dropped out. The events have all had a Trumpian flair, featuring appearances from his friends and the aim of showcasing spectacle, Americana and power.

In this latest case, it will be horsepower.

In addition to the main event, there was also a prerace show with flyovers of military aircraft, which swooped and boomed over the city during the July Fourth celebrations.

The IndyCar race comes as Trump has been struggling to resolve the war he started nearly six months ago with Iran, a conflict that has driven up gasoline prices and exacerbated worries from officials in his Republican Party that voters in this November’s midterm elections see the president as distracted and not focused enough on cost-of-living concerns.

Trump in his second term has increasingly seemed to focus on relishing the presidency’s ceremonial aspects. That's included a healthy dose of visits to sporting events — including an appearance last month at the World Cup final, where he presented the trophy to winner Spain and lingered onstage with the team as its members jumped in a hail of confetti.

An executive order Trump signed earlier this year calling for the Freedom 250 Grand Prix declared that the “cars and drivers inspire awe and respect in all who watch this quintessentially American sport,” and the event will “showcase the majesty of our great city as drivers navigate a track around our iconic national monuments in celebration of America’s 250th birthday.”

IndyCar series owner Roger Penske, a longtime friend of Trump’s who received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from him in 2019, helped lead the effort to bring the race to Washington.

Trump told Fox on Sunday that Penske told him that he had been trying to bring the race to Washington for 20 years.

“When he came to see Trump it got done in about 15 minutes and it’s turned out to be much bigger than we ever even thought possible,” the president said, referring to himself in the third person.

Bud Denker, president of Penske Corporation and the race’s chair, said that Penske is paying for the “vast majority” of the race, including building the track and road improvements, while the District of Columbia handled some repaving.

Both Penske and Denker met Trump when he arrived at the course. Trump and the first lady then met and chatted with some race drivers.

Among the changes needed on the city’s streets was the welding of more than 200 maintenance hole covers to ensure the race cars don’t suck them up off the road.

Sunday’s festivities are also the latest opportunity for Trump to revel in the way he’s putting his mark on the nation’s capital, including large banners showing his face on government buildings, the construction of a massive White House ballroom, a gold-adorned Oval Office and botched repairs at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

News.title: Newcastle vs Liverpool LIVE: Substitute Willock restores lead minutes after Gakpo equaliser
News.content:
( PA )

Newcastle host Liverpool in the Premier League’s late kick off this afternoon with both clubs having undergone managerial changes in the summer break.

Eddie Howe departed as Newcastle boss following the sales of Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon with his replacement Matthias Jaissle tasked with rebuilding the team this season. He faces a difficult opener with the Magpies winless in their last 19 top-flight encounters with Liverpool, though regime change at Anfield as well could present an opportunity to end that run.

Andoni Iraola takes charge of Liverpool having replaced Arne Slot. He will be hoping to bring the best out of Alexander Isak, who faces a hostile return to St James’ Park, and Florian Wirtz who underperformed in their first season with the Reds while also figuring out how exactly Liverpool can replace Mohamed Salah who has departed for Turkey. Iraola has himself admitted his squad was “thin” in some areas.

It is also set to be an emotional afternoon at St James’ Park as Newcastle and Liverpool join together to pay tribute to Kevin Keegan, who was a legendary figure at both clubs. Keegan passed away in July at the age of 75 and fans of both clubs will pay tribute before kick-off.

Follow all the action from St. James’ Park with our live blog below:

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat to Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guehi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass then City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: Norris wins incident-packed Dutch Grand Prix as Russell loses ground again
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris passed Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton in the space of a single lap before holding on to win the Dutch Grand Prix for back-to-back Formula One victories.

Norris started on pole but was overtaken by Antonelli at a restart after the race was stopped for a heavy crash by hometown driver Max Verstappen, who was unhurt, during the second lap.

Norris reeled in Antonelli before passing him around the outside of the first corner in a daring move on lap 54 of 72, then took the lead from Ferrari’s Hamilton before the lap was over.

The defending champion held on with old tyres to take the win. “This fight is still on,” he said over team radio.

“The move [to pass Antonelli] was good. I knew I was not going to get many chances. Every lap I spent behind him my chances got lower and lower,” Norris said. “Well played from my part...I probably had one chance.”

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

News.title: George Russell king of the sprint and driving with freedom after engagement
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix, the first race after F1’s summer break. Kimi Antonelli has had a tremendous first part of the season, leading Lewis Hamilton by 50 points and George Russell by 59 after the first 11 rounds. He has taken six wins to Russell’s two, with Hamilton, Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc all racking up a win apiece.

His start to the second part of the season was not the best, however. A messy sprint qualifying session meant he ended down in fifth, more than 0.2sec behind team-mate Russell, who took a much-needed pole.

Some of the damage was self-inflicted, quite literally. In the first session of sprint qualifying he ran wide at the banked turn 12 and into the gravel. The damage to the floor of his car was attempted to be repaired for the rest of the session but left him lacking downforce. A gap of 0.2sec is not enormous but the other issue was that three other cars – Norris, Leclerc and Piastri – are between him and Russell.

That said, it is not a great worry at this point. The points available in the sprint are relatively small and Antonelli has a healthy margin at this point over his rivals. In any case, there is no guarantee that Russell and Antonelli finish where they will start. Antonelli has shown on numerous occasions that he can bounce back from a difficult session and you have to expect that again here.

The race, which starts at 11am BST, is one-third of the race distance and should be run in dry conditions. There have been persistent showers and a steady breeze at Zandvoort this weekend, but it is not expected to affect the running in the sprint.

Qualifying for tomorrow’s grand prix comes later today at 3pm, which could be a more consequential session.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland’s girlfriend copies Man City star with her own haircut as she shows off new look
Sports.content:
ERLING HAALAND’s girlfriend has copied her partner and had a haircut.

The Manchester City striker surprised everyone when he chopped off his long locks ahead of the new season.



And now Wag Isabel Haugseng Johansen has shown off her own fresh trim.

Not going as extreme as Haaland, model Isabel went slightly shorter with her brown style.





She posted online wearing a black turtle neck in the seat of a car, writing: “A lil refresh for fall x”

Her hair now falls just below her shoulders having been down to the middle of her back before.

And fellow Norwegian Isabel gave a wink to the camera in her makeup.

The 22-year-old also posed in a video put on her story as she travelled in a plush vehicle to watch Haaland face Bournemouth.



He rocked a sharp buzz cut after binning off the pony tail in a shock to all.

Isabel was seen being driven in the back with white leather before she also took snaps from the stands at the Etihad.



Haaland blanked on opening day but City did come from behind to win 2-1.

His poor performance led some fans to beg him to regrow his hair, suggesting it held special goal scoring powers.

It was Enzo Maresca‘s first competitive match in charge with late goals from Marc Guehi and an overturned VAR strike from Josko Gvardiol sealing three points.

Haaland had a massive chance to put City ahead early on but scuffed his close-range effort.



He spent the summer at the World Cup with huge social media hit Isabel following him around.

She has over 2.1million Instagram followers and has been dating Haaland since his days at Borussia Dortmund.

Sports.title: Tottenham AGREE Omar Marmoush loan transfer with £50million option to buy after striking deal with Man City
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM have agreed to sign Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush on loan, reports say – and he could join permanently next season.

The winger was an unused sub for Enzo Maresca on opening day as his side came from behind to beat Bournemouth.



And Fabrizio Romano claims that a deal with City including a conditional obligation to buy for £50million has been struck just minutes after full-time.

Marmoush, 27, will now travel to London for his medical on Monday.



He will join fellow City attacker Savinho in making the big-money move to Spurs.

Marmoush will be bought by Spurs if certain, so far unknown, clauses are met.

Sports.title: Why are Newcastle and Liverpool players wearing black armbands?
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE and Liverpool kick off their Premier League campaigns with a huge clash at St James’ Park this afternoon.

Both sides are wearing black armbands in memory of footballing great Kevin Keegan.



Why are Newcastle and Liverpool players wearing black armbands?

Players and staff from both Newcastle and Liverpool are wearing black armbands in tribute to Keegan, who died aged 75 in July after a battle with cancer.

Keegan achieved legendary status at both clubs during his illustrious career as both a player and manager.





He scored 100 goals in 322 games during his time on Merseyside, helping Liverpool to three league titles, a European Cup, an FA Cup and two Uefa Cups during his time at the Reds.

Keegan, who won the Ballon d’Or twice during his time at German side Hamburg, ended his playing days at Newcastle.

The former England striker scored 49 times in 85 competitive appearances for the Magpies.

He helped the Toon secure promotion to the First Division in 1983/84 before calling time on his incredible career.



Eight years after retiring on Tyneside, Keegan returned to Newcastle as manager and helped save the club from relegation to the third tier for the first time in the club’s history.

After sealing promotion back to the First Division in his first full season in the St James’ Park dugout, he led the Magpies to the summit of English football.

Before this afternoon’s game, players warmed up in special shirts and a moving display by Wor Flags included both Newcastle and Liverpool supporters.

A minute’s applause also took place prior to kick-off on what will be a very emotional day for all concerned.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace prepare audacious £50m transfer bid to lure Jarrod Bowen back to Premier League amid West Ham nightmare
Sports.content:
CRYSTAL PALACE are preparing to launch an audacious £50million bid to lure Jarrod Bowen back to the Premier League.

The West Ham skipper, 29, pledged to stay at the club this season despite relegation to the Championship – and signed a new contract.



But that is not putting off Palace, who are preparing to sell current right winger Ismaila Sarr.

The Hammers’ financial woes are no secret – and selling their captain would go a long way towards easing that pressure.



It would also boost Bowen’s chances of breaking back into the England squad after being overlooked for the World Cup.

Palace, 2-0 opening weekend losers at Everton, want Bowen to replace Sarr, who is keen to leave for Galatasaray.

The Turkish giants are hopeful a £34m switch can be concluded next week.

Senegal winger Sarr, 28, wants Champions League football – and was left out of the Everton game by new Eagles boss Pierre Sage.

Sarr scored 21 goals for Palace last season, helping them win the Conference League.

Bowen managed only 11 in all competitions for West Ham, who went down on the last day of the season.

His departure would spark a huge fan backlash however as Nuno Espirito Santo’s side are winless in the Championship so far.

Taty Castellanos missed a stoppage-time penalty in yesterday’s 2-1 home defeat to Charlton, with supporters puzzled as to why Bowen did not take it.

Palace were frontrunners to sign Bowen from Hull in January 2020 – but it was West Ham who ended up paying £22m for him that month.

The Eagles will be looking to bounce back from their season-opening defeat to Everton when they face Manchester City on Friday.

Sports.title: Non-league star suffers horror facial fractures and left needing surgery after sickening challenge
Sports.content:
A NON-LEAGUE star is set to go under the knife after suffering a horror facial injury.

Dartford, who hosted a music event to celebrate 20 years at Princes Park, were condemned to a thumping 3-0 defeat by Welling United in the Isthmian Premier League yesterday.



And Joe Tennent had to be substituted in the first half of the Kent minnows’ heavy loss.

The defender, 28, was on the end of a sickening challenge from Welling man Nahum Melvin-Lambert.



Physios rushed to Tennent’s aid after he was immediately seen writhing in agony.

Dartford have shared footage of the incident, which led to Melvin-Lambert escaping with a booking, on social media.



And the Darts have released a statement confirming they are considering taking action as Tennent prepares for an operation.

It read: “Joe sustained displaced facial fractures and will undergo cheekbone reconstruction surgery on Wednesday.

“We wish Joe and his family our very best and a speedy recovery. The club will explore official channels following the incident.”

To make matters worse for Dartford, who have EFL icon Scott Wagstaff on their books, Melvin-Lambert went on to find the net in the second half.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Nathan Cooper and Fumnaya Shomotun were also on target as Welling bagged all three points.

Dartford player-boss Ben Greenhalgh, who won the Champions League with Inter Milan, reckons the injury was a huge turning point.

The ex-Como loanee, 34, said: “I think a really big, key part of today was losing Joe Tennent.

“He’s obviously taken whatever it was to his head. He’s got a possible broken jaw.

“It was a derby game so we knew there were going to be moments. I can’t blame the ref for the game. That has changed it but our second half performance was really poor.



“We lost Joe and I’m not saying we capitulated but we went a bit off-script.

Sports.title: Man City 2 Bournemouth 1: Josko Gvardiol scores dramatic injury-time winner as Maresca’s men complete late comeback
Sports.content:
NICK it at the death, after a nightmare afternoon.

Maybe Enzo Maresca has got the magic touch needed to deal with the shadow of Pep.



For 84 minutes at the Etihad, Maresca looked like a man who had walked into a deeper pool than he had ever imagined.

Hot on the heels of the embarrassment in Cardiff last week, City looked like a side questioning their new direction.



Self-inflicted blunders, poor selections and a tactical set-up that left many City supporters shaking their heads seemed set to add up to a first opening weekend home defeat since the club returned to the Prem nearly a quarter of a century ago.

Bournemouth, in front through Marcus Tavernier and superbly drilled, were that close to plunging City into further early-season misery.

Yet having got it all wrong from the start, with Marc Guehi an unconvincing midfield screen, Rico Lewis having one to forget and Phil Foden heading down the tunnel when he was hauled off, it all came up trumps for the new City boss.

Guehi had earlier missed an absolute sitter, somehow heading wide of a gaping target from a couple of yards.



That added to a series of misses by Erling Haaland, who had always previously netted on the opening weekend.

But the arrival of Rayan Cherki – making a clear statement when he was belatedly sent on – sparked the stunning turnaround.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

With time running out, it was Cherki’s inswinger from the right that found Guehi on his own, for a header that took a touch off Adrien Truffert on its way into the net.

And three minutes into added time, Cherki teased through, for Josko Gvardiol to find the net.

While the flag was instantly raised, it needed just one replay to signal the inevitable overturned decision, James Hill clearly playing the Croatian onside before he rolled past Djordje Petrovic.



Yet while salvation came in those last few minutes, what had preceded it suggested the burden of replacing a Prem managerial legend may be as tough for Maresca as it proved for David Moyes at United and Unai Emery in North London before him.

For now, the heat will subside. Three points, in any circumstances, tend to have that effect.

Maresca will have his new recruits, too, although expecting £85m teenager Ayyoud Bouaddi to replicate Rodri’s sense of control at the rudder is a big ask.

The Italian, of course, knows he can trust Haaland to come good as well – even if the Norwegian did an impression of Samson after Delilah lopped off his flowing locks.

When Haaland, with the goal at his mercy from Nico O’Reilly’s terrific early cross, got it all wrong and the ball bounce off his rib-cage, it was a shock.



Likewise, two second half misses, spooning one over the top and then scuffing a shot when Guehi pulled back, were signals that he is still feeling his way back after his summer exertions in the USA.

That could have been so costly after Bournemouth, with new boss Marco Rise sticking with Andoni Iraola’s set-up and a rope a dope strategy, almost pulled it off perfectly.

When Gigi Donnarumma pawed Rayan’s angled strike behind, it was a warning shot but one they failed to heed.

But when Abdukodir Khusanov barged into Evanilson rather than dealing with Adam Smith’s ball from right-back, the ball to fell to Rayan.



Evanilson, sensing the uncertainty, drifted right to receive and when he slid across, Tavernier had time – so much time, with Lewis horribly out of position – to slam home.

Haaland did force Petrovic to tip over but with Lewis miles off the pace again, it needed Donnarumma’s huge frame to deny Justin Kluivert a second before the interval.

The second half was more about Bournemouth defending yet City remained blunt.

Guehi simply had to score when Petrovic lost his footing from Foden’s corner before after Cherki was sent on, Antoine Semenyo’s low strike was kept out by Petrovic.

Then came those two Haaland misses before the late twist, handing the Cherries their first league defeat since Semenyo left them for City in January.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Maresca will hope that the new recruits ,means his side will get better, too, when they fully understand what is expected of them.

But he cannot keep putting square pegs in round holes and anticipate things all working out. Not in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Newcastle and Liverpool pay tribute to Kevin Keegan as they say goodbye to football legend at Premier League clash
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE and Liverpool came together with a touching tribute to legendary football star Kevin Keegan.

The two-time Ballon d’Or winner sadly died last month after a brave battle with stomach cancer.



Follow the latest updates from Newcastle vs Liverpool on our live blog

He had been diagnosed with stage four cancer in January after visiting the hospital for abdominal problems.



He passed away surrounded by family at the age of 75, kicking off waves of tributes around the country.

And now Liverpool and the Magpies, both of whom he became a legend for in his playing days, jointly expressed their condolences ahead of their Prem opener on Sunday.

Kenny Dalglish was among the stars to lay a wreath down outside the stadium in honour of his fellow Liverpool legend.

Alan Shearer and Stuart Pearce were also spotted taking in the pre-match tributes from the stands.



St James’ Park itself was filled with handouts featuring Keegan’s name and a heartfelt message from his family.

The stands were also decorated so as to feature his name when empty ahead of the match.



And the matchday programme was dedicated to him, featuring a snap of him as Newcastle manager on the cover.

The Keegan family released a letter to fans before the match that read: “Dear Newcastle United fans and the incredible city of Newcastle.

“The past couple of weeks have been some of the hardest that our family has endured, saying goodbye to our husband, father, and grandfather, Kevin.

“Despite living outside of the region, your love and warmth from the North East has reached our hearts and filled us with so much comfort during these difficult days.



“The empathy, compassion and warmth of this extraordinary club and community have shone through; the outpouring of love has been truly overwhelming.

“Kevin always shared his love for Newcastle United, Geordies, and the city, captivating us with stories told with his infectious smile.

“Seeing these tributes brought those stories to life for Kevin’s grandchildren, showing them how deeply their grandfather was loved in return.

“It also allowed us a quiet moment to reflect on many fond memories of Kevin’s incredible career and the incomparable bond he shared with Newcastle.



“Your football club, city, and community show a passion that truly embodied Kevin as a footballer, manager, and family man. We will be eternally grateful for the adoration and strength you have given our family when we needed it most.”

The players of Liverpool warmed up in kits featuring Keegan’s name and number seven, and a banner featuring his song alongside the word ‘legend’ was placed on the centre circle.



That was accompanied by a tifo featuring a number of photos of Keegan throughout his career as a player and a manager, alongside the caption “King Kev.”

Fans took the opportunity to display their own banners in the stands, including an iconic quote of his.

It read: “I want people to dream about their football club. They should. We should all be dreamers at heart.



“Some people are the opposite and say ‘we can’t do that,’ but when you ask them why, they can’t give a reason. Well I say ‘why not?'”

Manchester City also offered their condolences ahead of their Prem opener with Bournemouth at the Etihad.

Keegan managed the Citizens for four years in the early 2000s, finishing top of the second tier to earn the side promotion back to the Premier League.



Keegan made 230 league appearances for the Reds between 1971 and 1977, winning three first division titles and a European Cup.

He found himself in his native North East a few years later with Newcastle, where he would score 48 times in 78 league appearances in the early 80s.

But he is just as fondly remembered for his managerial career with the club as he is for his playing days.



Eight years after his departure as a player, Keegan returned to kick off his managerial career at St James’ Park, bringing the club back into the top tier under his watch.

There they competed against Manchester United for the Premier League title – and though Keegan never secured silverware with the club, he left a lasting legacy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The grief of the crowd made the moment all the more spectacular when Anthony Elanga gave the home side the lead after just four minutes of play.

The former Nottingham Forest man was released down the right wing by William Osula, and made no mistake firing low across goal to the far post.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca dodges early Man City question as late show spares his blushes
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca dodges early Man City question as late show spares his blushes

MANCHESTER CITY 2-1: BOURNEMOUTH: Enzo Maresca was facing an embarrassing defeat on his first Manchester City outing before two late goals as the Italian seeks to fill the huge void left by Pep Guardiola

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca's Man City tenure began with a win

Had Pep Guardiola masterminded this comeback win, he would have been hailed a genius again. But Enzo Maresca still has a long, long way to go before earning comparisons to the bloke he has replaced.

‌



In the meantime, Maresca will just be relieved to have got his first positive result on the board, however difficult it was to get. For more than 84 minutes Manchester City appeared to be heading towards the kind of defeat which would have raised serious questions about Maresca's ability to fill the gigantic shoes of Guardiola.

‌



Marcus Tavernier had put Bournemouth ahead before half time, sending most of the Etihad into silence. And despite dominating possession, City offered little in the way of a fightback, aside from some bad misses from Erling Haaland and Marc Guehi.

‌



But thanks to bit of luck and the introduction of Rayan Cherki, Maresca's men somehow snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Guehi's deflected header from Cherki's corner levelled the scores, before Cherki's clever pass allowed Josko Gvardiol to snatch the winner in stoppage time. And breathe, Enzo.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Fresh off a thrashing from Arsenal in the Community Shield, City begun their league campaign knowing the visit of Bournemouth carried a bit more significance. Starting with a home defeat to a team you'd trounced by an aggregate score of 34-6 in nine previous home wins, was unthinkable.

‌



Not least when Maresca had rolled the dice and picked two of his stars in unorthodox positions, with Guehi operating as a defensive midfielder and Nico O'Reilly starting in the No.10 role. Visiting boss Marco Rose was also starting a new job, and handed a debut to Antonio Silva following his arrival from Benfica.

City started well and ripped into Bournemouth. Haaland tore through midfield to help create a chance for Rico Lewis, but his shot was well saved by Dorde Petrovic. O'Reilly had a free header from the resulting corner, but sent it onto the roof of the net, before Phil Foden had a shot blocked.

View 2 Images Josko Gvardiol scored in stoppage time to down Bournemouth

‌



Haaland then blew a golden chance, fluffing a cross from O'Reilly after the England international had charged half the length of the field before picking him out to perfection. The blunder looked even worse on 26 minutes, when Rose's men went ahead.

It was their first real attack of the game, but a clinical one. City failed to deal with a long ball forward, allowing Rayan to turn sharply and pick out Evanilson, who delivered a sublime cross which Tavernier converted at the back post. Cue silence in most parts of the ground.

It took a crucial interception from Gvardiol to stop Rayan from having a clear run on goal, as City continued to wobble. Petrovic scrambled to his left to keep out a header from Haaland, but the visitors were looking the most dangerous. Tavernier curled a strike just wide and Gianluigi Donnarumma did well to deny Justin Kluivert.

‌



A rumpus on the stroke of half time summed up City's frustrations. That feeling got worse when Guehi missed an absolute sitter from close range, when it looked easier to score.

City needed a spark and Guehi provided one, equalising with five minutes remaining to make amends, before Gvardiol completed the fightback. But it could still promise to be a long season for Maresca. Provided he survives to the end of it, of course.

Sports.title: Newcastle pay touching tribute to late Kevin Keegan alongside Liverpool as family thank club
Sports.content:
Newcastle pay touching tribute to late Kevin Keegan alongside Liverpool as family thank club

Newcastle United and Liverpool paid tribute to the late Kevin Keegan ahead of their Premier League clash at St James' Park on Sunday, with the family of the legendary manager giving their thanks

View 5 Images Tributes were shown to Kevin Keegan in Newcastle (Image: Sky Sports)

Newcastle United gave an emotional tribute to the late Kevin Keegan at St James' Park on Sunday afternoon ahead of their Premier League opener with Liverpool. The legendary former footballer and manager died at the age of 75 last month following a battle with cancer, with tributes pouring in across the world of sport.

‌



And given the Armthorpe-born icon represented the Magpies both as a player and a manager, as well as Liverpool during his playing days, the clubs felt it was only right that they afforded him an emotional send-off ahead of their first English top flight outing of 2026/27.

‌



On top of the players warming up in shirts adorned with Keegan's iconic number seven, 500 shirts were laid in a mosaic reading 'legend' and 'There's only one Kevin Keegan,' in the centre circle of the stadium. Bobby Moncur, Ian Rush, Shola Ameobi and Sir Kenny Dalglish also laid wreaths in the Newcastle memorial gardens ahead of Sunday's 4.30pm kick-off on Tyneside.

‌



Kevin Keegan's cause of death as Liverpool and Newcastle prepare to pay tribute READ MORE :

A letter from Keegan's family was also included in the pre-match programme, in which fans were thanked for their support over an incredibly tough period. It read: "Dear Newcastle United fans and the incredible city of Newcastle.

"The past couple of weeks have been some of the hardest that our family has endured, saying goodbye to our husband, father, and grandfather, Kevin. Despite living outside of the region, your love and warmth from the North East has reached our hearts and filled us with so much comfort during these difficult days.

"The empathy, compassion and warmth of this extraordinary club and community have shone through; the outpouring of love has been truly overwhelming. Having seen the tributes outside St. James’ Park, members of our family came home to Newcastle to see the memorials in person.

‌



"The sea of black and white shirts and scarves, alongside colours from so many other clubs, reminded us how much Kevin meant to the footballing world. It was a sombre moment that reminded us of our pain and loss, yet matched with immense pride and love as we read so many personal and heartfelt messages.

View 5 Images Former Newcastle and Liverpool players laid wreathes (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

"Kevin always shared his love for Newcastle United, Geordies, and the city, captivating us with stories told with his infectious smile. Seeing these tributes brought those stories to life for Kevin’s grandchildren, showing them how deeply their grandfather was loved in return.

‌



"It also allowed us a quiet moment to reflect on many fond memories of Kevin’s incredible career and the incomparable bond he shared with Newcastle. Your football club, city, and community show a passion that truly embodied Kevin as a footballer, manager, and family man.

"We will be eternally grateful for the adoration and strength you have given our family when we needed it most. Newcastle, thank you for your love. The Keegan Family."

Placards were also left on seats around St James' Park for fans to hold up in the build-up to kick-off, adorned with instructions and the words "Long live the king." Wor Flags also provided a display of Keegan's name in red in the Liverpool section of Level Seven, while the number seven sat below among the home fans.

‌



View 5 Images Placards were left for fans inside St James' Park (Image: Getty Images)

The Newcastle-based organisation also erected a one-off tifo which showed a collage of Keegan from his time at Newcastle United as both a player and a manager, as well as the words "King Kev." Meanwhile, fans held banners in the stands, showing Keegan's iconic "we should all be dreamers message."

A minute of applause was also given for Keegan as kick-off fast approached, with both sets of supporters, as well as the likes od Dalglish and Alan Shearer joining in. A two-time Ballon d'Or winner, Keegan kicked off his footballing career at Scunthorpe United in 1968, spending three years with the club before a move to Liverpool arrived.

‌



View 5 Images Newcastle and Liverpool fans paid tribute to Keegan (Image: Sky Sports)

After spending six years with the Reds, he moved onto Hamburger SV, before returning to English soil with Southampton in 1980. Keegan arrived at St James' Park in 2982, enjoying a two-year stint with the club before seeing out the last year of his career at Blacktown City.

In a trophy-laden playing career, Keegan won the First Division title with Liverpool three times, as well as the European Cup and a pair of UEFA Cups. He also won a Bundesliga title with Hamburg. Keegan then stepped into the world of management in 1992 with Newcastle, guiding the club to a First Division (now Championship) title in his maiden season.

‌



View 5 Images Keegan was a club legend for Newcastle and Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

After five years at the helm, Keegan moved onto Fulham for two years, and enjoyed short stints with England and Manchester City before one last dance with the Magpies in 2008.

Sports.title: Aston Villa's overhaul exposed as Unai Emery's new era has worst possible start
Sports.content:
Aston Villa's overhaul exposed as Unai Emery's new era has worst possible start

BRIGHTON 4-0 ASTON VILLA: Unai Emery's new look side endured the worst possible start to their Premier League season as they were hammered on the south coast

View 2 Images Unai Emery's new look Aston Villa side were destroyed at Brighton

If you're going to sell six of the XI who helped you win a first trophy in 30 years, then you'd better show why. Aston Villa's opening game only served to suggest that the timing of their mass overhaul may have been a little premature.

‌



Unai Emery stood on the touchline at the Amex and saw his Europa League champions trailing 4-0 inside 31 minutes. His defence, minus Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, were the architects of their own downfall. Brighton were able to take advantage of Villa giving the ball away in their own box to score two of their four goals.

‌



Emery could not rely on Youri Tielemans to get control of the game - he's gone. He couldn't turn to Morgan Rogers to try and produce a moment of individual magic - he's gone.

‌



Emery couldn't ask Ollie Watkins to run in behind and stretch the Brighton defence - he was left out and looks like he's off to Saudi Arabia.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The succession planning beyond Watkins is not exactly in place. There's talk of a move for Nicolas Jackson, but with Watkins omitted, Emery had to start with no recognised No.9 in his line-up. Emi Buendia was tasked with leading the line.

‌



Joao Gomes, the man who is serving as the replacement for Tielemans, didn't even last 45 minutes as he was shown a red card on debut.

By the time he was dismissed the game was effectively over. Victor Lindelof, who started less than a third of games last term and would likely be on the bench if Konsa was still present, put through his own net inside 10 minutes. Maxim De Cuyper tapped home to double the Brighton lead and Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in two minutes, which saw some Villa fans in the away end head for the exits.

View 2 Images Aston Villa have lost more than half of last year's team, raising questions over the timing of their overhaul

‌



Villa's summer business has been in part driven by a need to remain financially compliant. That said, rarely, if ever, has history shown that ripping up a team who finished fourth and won a European trophy is a good idea, especially in the short term.

We haven't even mentioned Emi Martinez, who was left out after another summer where he's been linked with the exit door. The Argentine's move to Juventus fell through recently and Villa have already moved for life after Martinez, signing Zion Suzuki from Parma.

Before kick-off, Emery claimed his Villa side were "motivated, we are so excited". It must be said that the Midlands outfit have suffered opening weekend hammerings in the past - losing 5-1 at Newcastle in 2023 before going on to finish fourth.

Article continues below

That was under very different circumstances though and with a team that enjoyed continuity. Emery is the one constant at Villa, and the Spaniard has continually outperformed his resources at Villa Park, but those resources may have been gutted to an extent that even his magic wand is limited.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick snaps at reporter for 'ridiculous' Man Utd question after Hull defeat
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick snaps at reporter for 'ridiculous' Man Utd question after Hull defeat

Manchester United lost their opening game of the Premier League season against newly promoted Hull and Michael Carrick wasn't happy with some of the criticism levelled at his players

View 2 Images Michael Carrick took umbrage with a question (Image: MUTV)

Unhappy Michael Carrick snapped at a reporter who asked if Manchester United lacked 'passion' during their woeful 2-0 loss away to Hull. The Red Devils got their Premier League campaign off to a wretched start against the side tipped to finish bottom of the table.

‌



Captain Bruno Fernandes bemoaned United's habit of giving the ball away cheaply while left-back Luke Shaw admitted that they hadn't prepared properly. Premier League legend Alan Shearer even accused Carrick's players of looking 'unfit'.

‌



Post-match, Carrick was interviewed by ex-Middlesbrough striker Jan Age Fjortoft, who was working for broadcaster Viaplay at the MKM Stadium. Fjortoft questioned United's passion in the first half, to which Carrick furrowed his brow and replied: "Come on, that's ridiculous.

‌



"You played football, you understand. That's a ridiculous thing to say. Just because you get beaten doesn't mean you don't care about it.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Their two goals came from set plays. Other than that, we had opportunities. That was where the game was. I don't think it was passion or anything to do with that. It was just their moments that made the difference in the game."

Indeed Hull's goals did some from set pieces, as Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy put the hosts two goals to the good before half-time. United brought on Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko in search for comeback, but Hull - much thanks to goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis - kept them at bay.

Was Michael Carrick's reaction justified? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick and his players have been criticised (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Carrick insists that United won't be 'rocked' by the result and will 'stay in the bubble' ahead their first home game against Ipswich, who were also promoted from the Championship last season. "It's one game. It's the first game of the season so it's disappointing enough and it hurts, of course it does," the Red Devils boss emphasised.

"But it's one game, it doesn't change the whole course of the direction the team or the football club is going in. We'll stay calm, stay in the bubble and focus on next week."

Article continues below

Carrick could have a new signing at his disposal come next Sunday, with United having agreed a £70m deal with Brighton for midfielder Carlos Baleba. But Carrick wasn't giving anything away, saying: "I had all eyes on this [game] today, so any other player, at any other club… until he's ours, it's not for me to comment on that."

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli poised to hand Arsenal huge payday as £60m transfer option emerges
Sports.content:
Gabriel Martinelli poised to hand Arsenal huge payday as £60m transfer option emerges

Arsenal are in talks over a potential deal for Gabriel Martinelli, with the Brazilian slipping down the pecking order following Christos Tzolis' summer arrival

View Image Gabriel Martinelli could leave Arsenal before the transfer deadline day (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal are holding discussions with Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal over a potential transfer for Gabriel Martinelli. The Brazilian has slipped out of favour under Mikel Arteta and the club are prepared to consider offers if their asking price is met.

‌



Martinelli has been consistently linked with a move away from the Premier League champions this summer. Galatasaray held talks earlier this month, while AS Roma have also expressed interest in the 25‑year‑old.

‌



The Athletic now report that Al Hilal are actively pursuing a deal and are in discussions with Martinelli’s representatives over a prospective move. Arsenal are believed to be seeking around £60million.

‌



11 top Premier League players in final year of contract including Man Utd and Liverpool stars READ MORE :

While no deal has been struck, talks are continuing - and Martinelli is understood to be receptive to the prospect of playing in Saudi Arabia.

He finds himself at a career crossroads, with regular first-team football in north London appearing improbable following the arrival of Christos Tzolis and Arsenal's efforts to recruit another forward, with Julian Alvarez amongst those linked.

Mikel Arteta omitted Martinelli from his matchday squads for both the Community Shield and the home victory over Coventry City on Friday night.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal legend Ian Wright has confessed he feels 'uncomfortable' with the manner in which Martinelli is being handled. "With respect to Martinelli and the way he's being treated at the moment, it really makes me uncomfortable," he told Sky Sports.

"He always gives 100%, we're not saying he's the greatest, but he's come up with some big moments for Arsenal in big games, and the way he's being treated at the end here.

‌



"I know they might want him out and there's a lot of guys saying it's time for him to move on, but there's ways of doing that should suit him as well."

Martinelli has 12 months remaining on his existing contract, and while Arsenal possess an option to prolong it by another year, triggering that clause now seems improbable. The winger joined the Emirates Stadium in 2019, arriving from Brazilian outfit Ituano in a £6m transfer.

Arsenal are also prepared to part ways with Gabriel Jesus, with the Brazil international anticipated to depart as a free agent at the conclusion of the season should he fail to secure a transfer this summer or in January.

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins edges closer to Saudi Arabia transfer as he's left out of Aston Villa squad
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins edges closer to Saudi Arabia transfer as he's left out of Aston Villa squad

England and Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins looks set for a move to Saudi Arabia after being omitted from the club’s squad for their Premier League opener against Brighton & Hove Albion

View 2 Images Watkins has been left out of the Villa side to take on Brighton (Image: Getty Images)

Ollie Watkins has been axed from Aston Villa’s squad amid interest from Saudi Arabia. Watkins, 30, has been linked with a switch to Al-Hilal, with numerous bids having been turned down for the frontman.

‌



Villa however have now hinted that his future might lie away from the Midlands. Watkins has been left out of the club’s 18-man squad that will take on Brighton & Hove Albion in their Premier League opener on Sunday, with midfielder Emi Buendia instead selected to lead the line for Unai Emery’s side.

‌



Speaking in his pre-match press conference, the Villa boss insisted that he was not keen on selling Watkins. He said: "We have an issue with him, it's clear. He is our player. We have had offers for him.

‌



"I don't want to sell him but it can change because if it's a good option for him and the club and I can replace him in the squad, this is the routine we have and we did before with the players who are leaving.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"With Ollie, he is here, for me he is a fantastic striker, we have always believed in him. Now he is our player, there are 10 days more or less to finish the transfer window, we will see what happens, I'm happy with him, if he is staying with us he will continue playing his level."

‌



When asked by Sky Sports prior to Villa's game against Newcastle whether Watkins' absence meant he had played his last game for the club, Emery simply replied: "Silence."

Watkins still has two years left to run on his contract with Villa, having arrived at the club from Brentford back in 2020. Since then, he has gone on to make 278 appearances for the side and has scored 108 goals - many of which have helped the club win the Europa League in the summer, as well as to three seasons in Europe.

Watkins has also become a full international during his spell with Villa, having earned 24 caps for England and scored seven times. Should his move to the Middle East go through, Watkins would become the latest high-profile star to leave the club this summer.

‌



View 2 Images Emery is keen on keeping hold of Watkins (Image: Getty Images)

Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea in a big-money move earlier this summer, while Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa have joined Manchester United and Arsenal respectively. Lucas Digne has also left, having rejoined former club Paris Saint-Germain.

Villa have attempted to rebuild their side in the aftermath of their summer exodus, with big-money swoops for Johan Manzambi and Joao Gomes, while they also completed a double deal for Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki earlier this week.

Article continues below

Alejandro Garnacho and Aaron Wan-Bissaka have also arrived on loan moves from Chelsea and West Ham.

Sports.title: Man City agree £85m transfer deal for World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi to replace Rodri
Sports.content:
Man City agree £85m transfer deal for World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi to replace Rodri

Enzo Maresca said this week that Manchester City need to find the 'new Rodri' after he joined Barcelona for £65million, and Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi was identified as his successor

View 2 Images Ayyoub Bouaddi is joining Manchester City (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Manchester City have landed Morocco superstar Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a deal costing up to £85million. Both clubs agreed the fee following extensive talks, with Bouaddi signing a five-year-deal at the Etihad with the option of an extra 12 months.

‌



The move will take City's summer spending through the £200m barrier. The initial fee will be £81.4m, rising to £85m over the course of Bouaddi's time in the blue half of Manchester.

‌



Bouaddi, 18, has emerged as one of the most talented and exciting teenagers in world football. City chiefs kept close tabs on his progress at this summer's World Cup, once it became clear Rodri would be leaving to join Barcelona.

‌



Bouaddi, who will be unveiled this week, impressed at the tournament, starting five of Morocco's six matches in their run to the last eight. City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak has been impressed with how Bouaddi has been able to step up on the big occasions as his burgeoning career has developed.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Senior club figures believe Bouaddi's ability to remain unfazed and be able to compete against more senior and experienced players makes him an ideal fit for the City team. Before the World Cup, Bouaddi had a starring role in Lille's shock Champions League win over Real Madrid in 2024, when he announced himself onto the big stage.

New City boss Enzo Maresca regards Bouaddi as the ideal, long-term replacement for Bernardo Silva, who joined Real Madrid at the end of last season. Bouaddi has made 88 appearances for Lille since making his debut in October 2023, three days after turning 16, and helped them finish third in Ligue One last season.

Is Ayyoub Bouaddi good enough to replace Rodri? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Ayyoub Bouaddi for Morocco impressed at the World Cup (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

He also broke a record held by Eden Hazard, after making 50 Ligue 1 appearances for Lille at the age of just 18. City are still keen to sign a direct replacement for holding midfielder Rodri, but talks with Chelsea about a deal for Enzo Fernandez have continued to stall.

Sports.title: 'Ask him' - Emery cryptic on Watkins amid transfer interest
Sports.content:
Unai Emery gave a coy and cryptic response to questions about Ollie Watkins' absence from Aston Villa's squad for their Premier League defeat at Brighton.

The striker did not travel to the Amex amid transfer interest from Al Hilal. Watkins is keen on the move to Saudi Arabia and Al Hilal have seen at least one bid rejected.

Villa do not want to sell Watkins but talks between the clubs continue.

Watkins returned from his post-World Cup summer break in the week before the game, but, when asked to explain whether his absence was due to physical or transfer-related reasons, Emery said: "Ask him. I only can answer it by silence."

That followed a pre-match interview, where Emery was asked about Watkins and, after a long pause, simply said: "Silence".

Post-match, Emery made reference to the "commitment" of his other players, despite Villa losing 4-0 and having Joao Gomes sent off in the first half at Brighton.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brighton and Aston Villa

Emery's exchange with Sky Sports reporter Johnny Phillips in full:

Can you clarify why Watkins wasn't in the squad today?

"This question is for him.

"Can you call him and make a question to him?"

So it was not your decision, it was his decision?

"Ask him. I only can answer it by silence."

Does this make it a challenging situation if it's not in your control?

"The players that are here, they showed it, their commitment and it's really fantastic and this is the way. Of course losing, but this is the way."

Is it disappointing to see it ending like this?

"We know, we had it before here. We had it in different moments. In four years we had it maybe five times in different circumstances.

"But we are going forward, moving always forward. My responsibility is to try to analyse, to find solutions and for the transfer window we have 10 days to find solutions, and we have then of course a way to find solutions with the players we have and we are doing [that].

"We did a fantastic match against PSG in the only official match we played, and today the first 10-15 minutes and the second half how we responded through our commitment, through our keeping up our focus and motivation, this is the best response I can find today. And then try to continue to find solution tactically and find solution with some needs in the squad. We always recover and came back from situations like that and I'm confident we will now."

Sports.title: Norris beats Antonelli to victory in Dutch GP
Sports.content:
Lando Norris outduelled championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second successive race victory by winning the Dutch Grand Prix.

McLaren's Norris started on pole in Zandvoort but lost the lead to Antonelli at an early standing restart after Red Bull's Max Verstappen triggered a red flag at his home race by crashing out at the end of the first lap.

After struggling to pressure Antonelli on the first stint, Norris was far quicker after switching onto a hard tyre at the first round of pit stops, and eventually passed the Mercedes after emerging from his second stop with far fresher tyres than the Italian.

Mercedes left George Russell vulnerable to missing out on a podium by ordering him to let Antonelli through to second in the closing stages, but the Brit was ultimately just able to hold off Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton for third.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen loses control of his car at the beginning of the race and hits the wall

Antonelli's championship lead grows to 59 points with Russell taking over second from Hamilton in the standings despite the pair having the same points total, while reigning champion Norris reduces his deficit to the leader to 83 points.

Reigning constructors' champions McLaren failed to claim a win in the opening 10 grands prix of the season, but a significant upgrade brought to the final round before the summer break in Hungary propelled Norris to a dominant success in Budapest.

Dutch GP Result: Top 10 1) Lando Norris, McLaren



2) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



3) George Russell, Mercedes



4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



5) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



6) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



7) Liam Lawson, Red Bull



8) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi



9) Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin



10) Pierre Gasly, Alpine

Had it not been for Norris giving up the lead with a poor getaway at the early restart, this victory could have been similarly dominant, leaving little doubt that the Brit appears the driver most likely to challenge Antonelli for the title over the remaining 11 rounds despite his current position of fourth in the standings.

Celebrating his victory over team radio moments after taking the chequered flag, Norris declared: "Let's keep bringing upgrades. Let's keep bringing performance. The fight is still on. Let's keep going."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris hunted down Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton to take the race lead

Charles Leclerc was fifth for Ferrari, whose pitwall endured a nervy final lap as their cars almost collided when the Monegasque closed up on the battle between Hamilton and Russell.

Oscar Piastri, who remains unable to come anywhere close to matching the pace of his team-mate Norris, was sixth.

Liam Lawson, deputising as Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate in place of the injured Isack Hadjar, completed a solid weekend by taking seventh.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ferrari team-mates nearly came together in the final stages of the race

Nico Hulkenberg, who did brilliantly to avoid a shunt with his Audi team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto on the first lap when the Brazilian spun just metres behind the Verstappen crash, made the most of the escape to take eighth.

Fernando Alonso exhibited Aston Martin's improvement following upgrades to both their chassis and Honda power unit by managing his tyres brilliantly on a one-stop strategy to claim ninth, while Pierre Gasly took the final point for Alpine.
