World.title: Baghdad hosts Iraqi-Libyan Joint Committee meetings after 25-year hiatus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Libya’s Acting Foreign Minister Taher al-Baour is in Baghdad heading a high-level delegation to co-chair the Iraqi-Libyan Joint Committee meetings, which have resumed after a 25-year break.

Al-Baour met with Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein to discuss strategies to enhance political, diplomatic, and regional ties between Baghdad and Tripoli.

Their discussions focused on aligning mutual political positions on regional problems and increasing combined consular and diplomatic presence.

Following their meeting, al-Baour and Hussein held a joint press conference. Al-Baour emphasized Libya’s immediate need to partner with Iraq to repair and staff key public facilities, particularly in education and healthcare.

The Libyan delegation is finalizing several memoranda of understanding covering a wide range of economic and development areas.

Al-Baour’s team includes officials from several government bodies affiliated with the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity (GNU).

According to the Iraqi Foreign Ministry, this diplomatic drive follows Iraq’s offer to resume coordination and signify a return to normalized, regular diplomatic ties between the two countries.

The delegation’s trip to Baghdad builds directly upon virtual expert meetings organized by the Libyan Ministry of Foreign Affairs to conclude trade agreements with Iraqi officials before signatures are authorized.

World.title: Japanese archaeological missions to return to Iraq for excavations and training
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Japanese archaeological excavation teams are preparing to return to Iraq to conduct scientific digs and provide hands-on field training for local researchers, according to statements made on Sunday, August 23, 2026, by Dr. Laith Majeed Hussein, Director of the Japanese–Iraqi Institute for Archaeological Education.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Hussein outlined that bilateral cooperation is expanding beyond field excavation to encompass academic faculty recruitment from Japan and Egypt to support the Department of Japanese Language and Literature at the University of Baghdad’s College of Arts.

Key Academic Initiatives & Archaeological Milestones

Resumption of Japanese Excavation Missions: Japanese archaeological teams—holding a multi-decade legacy of Mesopotamian field research—are coordinating their return following improvements in domestic security conditions to resume field surveying, artifact conservation, and joint research.

Hands-on Field Training: Upcoming excavation seasons will integrate joint fieldwork, pairing Japanese specialists and university students with Iraqi researchers and trainees to teach modern stratigraphic excavation and surveying methods.

Expansion of Japanese Language Studies: To build language proficiency and strengthen cultural exchange, the University of Baghdad’s College of Arts is recruiting native instructors and specialized faculty from Japan and Egypt to teach within its Japanese Language Department.

Institutional Heritage Ties: Dr. Hussein highlighted the historical roots of bilateral academic engagement, citing the establishment of the Center for the Revival of Arab Scientific Heritage in Baghdad in 1977, founded in close partnership with Japanese academic institutions.

International Assyriology Conference: Hussein noted that Baghdad had finalized preparations to host the 2026 Rencontre Assyriologique Internationale (International Congress of Assyriology); however, regional security tensions prompted a postponement, with organizers preparing to reapply for international convening approvals for a future date.

The revival of Japanese archaeological missions reflects the broader international reintegration of Iraq’s academic and heritage institutions.

By combining field excavations with university-level language instruction and peer-reviewed publishing partnerships, the Japanese–Iraqi Institute for Archaeological Education aims to equip a new generation of Iraqi scholars with advanced excavation methodologies and promote the preservation of Mesopotamian cultural heritage.

World.title: Economist: Iran Hormuz permits ‘too late’ as tankers secure safe passage
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi economic expert Ziyad Al-Hashemi stated on Saturday, August 22, 2026, that international crude buyers have successfully expanded oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz independently, making Tehran’s recent exceptional passage permits redundant.

According to Al-Hashemi’s analysis, published on social media and reported by regional news platforms, maritime tracking indicators show that commercial operators adapted to regional security risks days before official Iranian clearances were publicized. Consequently, he described Tehran’s formal approval as a late public-relations gesture aimed at courting the Iraqi public rather than a decisive logistical breakthrough.

Maritime Analytics & Key Operational Metrics

1 to 2 Million BPD Flowing: Energy market and maritime analytics from Vortexa confirm that seaborne crude volumes traversing the Strait of Hormuz averaged between 1 million and 2 million barrels per day (bpd) over the past 10 days, primarily originating from Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

Regional Total Reaching 3M BPD: Adding daily crude and fuel consignments from Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates, total maritime throughput across the waterway reached approximately 3 million bpd.

Adoption of “Dark Sailings”: Energy trading firms and shipping lines adapted by deploying smaller tankers and executing “dark sailings”—turning off or minimizing Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders—to obscure vessel positions and reduce targeting risks during transit.

Declining Maritime Attacks: Despite an increase in passing tanker traffic, maritime incidents and Iranian interdictions declined notably over the same period, signaling either altered strategic calculations regarding the Strait of Hormuz or diminished operational capacity to sustain maritime disruption.

Diminished Strategic Value of Permits: Because international buyers and shipping syndicates had already established functional transit routines, Al-Hashemi noted that Tehran’s publicized approvals arrived after navigational flows had already stabilized.

The analysis follows recent diplomatic and security discussions held in Baghdad between Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Iraqi officials, during which Tehran agreed to grant exceptional passage permits to designated Iraqi crude tankers navigating the chokepoint.

While state-level agreements sought to address maritime concerns, real-time energy flow tracking indicates that commercial charterers and global energy buyers utilized operational workarounds and alternative navigation protocols to maintain southern crude flows out of Basra’s offshore terminals.

World.title: 17th Agricultural Week opens in Baghdad: 30M date palm plan and tech deals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The 17th Agricultural Week Exhibition for agricultural mechanization, animal production, and food processing officially launched at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds on Saturday, August 22, 2026.

Operating under the theme “Supporting Agriculture to Harvest a Sustainable Future,” the exhibition hosts public- and private-sector pavilions featuring 209 local and international agricultural enterprises showcasing modern farming technology, climate-resilient crop inputs, and livestock pharmaceuticals.

Key Regional Partnerships & Technological Initiatives

1. Saudi-Iraqi Plant Biotechnology & Date Palm Expansion

30 Million Palm Target: Plant tissue culture specialist Saleh Al-Tuwaijri announced a strategic initiative to expand Iraq’s date palm population from approximately 20 million to 30 million trees.

Five-Year Production Capacity: Advanced tissue culture propagation techniques are projected to fulfill 30% to 40% of Iraq’s total seedling requirements over the next five years.

Domestic Biotechnology Labs: With logistical coordination from the Iraqi Ministries of Agriculture and Trade, the Saudi firm finalized the establishment of a specialized plant tissue culture laboratory inside Iraq.

Executive Backing: Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi, accompanied by the Ministers of Agriculture and Trade, toured the biotechnology pavilion during the exhibition to inspect progress and confirm state support.

2. Climate-Resilient Agricultural Solutions (Debbane – Lebanon)

Field Support & Climate Adaptation: Bassem Mohammed Hassan Al-Amin, Director General of Lebanon’s Debbane Modern Agriculture, highlighted that ongoing climate change necessitates specialized heat- and drought-tolerant seeds and soil fertilizers.

Agronomic Field Consulting: Engineering teams are deployed across Iraqi farmlands to deliver on-site technical guidance to optimize seasonal crop yields.

3. Livestock & Veterinary Pharmaceuticals (Syria)

Aviation & Cattle Sector Growth: Ammar Mohammed Al-Qazwini, Director General of the Arab Company for Veterinary Medicine Industries (Syria), noted Iraq’s expanding poultry operations, commercial dairy farms, and feed manufacturing infrastructure.

Cross-Border Veterinary Expertise: Syrian pharmaceutical manufacturers are providing advanced veterinary medicines and poultry treatments to boost local livestock productivity.

The 17th Agricultural Week serves as a regional conduit for introducing climate-adaptive biotechnology, localized seed breeding, and livestock healthcare into Iraq’s domestic farming ecosystem.

By facilitating cross-border investments and establishing domestic biotechnology laboratories, Iraq seeks to strengthen its national date palm reserves, reduce agricultural import dependency, and enhance long-term food security amid ongoing regional climate challenges.

World.title: Iraqi, Saudi ministers discuss energy security, economic integration
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair and Finance Minister Faleh al-Sari met with Saudi Energy Minister Abdulaziz bin Salman and Finance Minister Mohammed al-Jadaan in Riyadh on Friday to discuss energy security and economic integration.

The two sides discussed prospects of joint cooperation in the electricity, energy, and gas sectors to achieve the common interests of both Iraq and Saudi Arabia, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Oil Ministry.

The high-level discussions focused on increasing bilateral commerce, stabilizing regional oil supply, and developing an integrated energy infrastructure.

As Iraq plans to increase its oil output from four million barrels per day to between 8 and 10 million barrels per day over the next few years, the Iraqi delegation sought Saudi Arabia’s support to modify its OPEC output share.

The ministers agreed on the next measures to boost cross-border cooperation in the gas, electricity, and power distribution sectors, as well as to improve Iraq’s domestic grid efficiency.

The Iraqi officials indicated that the government is adopting a strategy to reduce dependency on the Strait of Hormuz. The country’s plans include increasing flows through Turkey’s Ceyhan port and exploring alternate transportation routes via Jordan’s Aqaba and Syria’s Baniyas.

The two sides discussed regional security developments, underscoring their shared commitment to sustaining global energy market stability and supply resilience.

World.title: Telecom Minister denies direct starlink deal, confirms EarthLink role
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Jabbar Sanad clarified on Saturday, August 22, 2026, that the Ministry has not signed a direct operational contract with U.S. satellite internet provider Starlink, affirming that domestic telecommunications provider EarthLink remains the state’s primary operational partner under existing service frameworks.

Speaking during a panel session at the 8th Baghdad Dialogue Conference, organized by the Iraqi Institute for Dialogue, Sanad stated that the Ministry seeks to harness market competition to upgrade the country’s digital infrastructure. He noted that while EarthLink and other entities currently provide connectivity, Starlink is slated to transition into a direct partnership role within two years.

Regulatory Oversight and Security Compliance

Participating in the same session, Baligh Abu Kalal, Head of the Communications and Media Commission (CMC), detailed the regulatory and security framework governing satellite internet deployment in Iraq:

Unregulated Terminals: An estimated 40,000 unauthorized Starlink devices were active across Iraq prior to formal regulatory engagement.

National Security Annex: Iraq established a comprehensive security regulatory appendix, making Starlink the first international satellite provider to formally subject its technical operations to Iraqi legal jurisdiction and national security specifications.

Global Precedent: Abu Kalal highlighted that Starlink services operate legally across more than 160 countries worldwide under comparable regulatory frameworks.

Formal Licensing Background: The clarification follows the CMC’s July announcement in the United States—held at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce—confirming the finalization of Starlink’s regulatory license to operate legally within the Iraqi market.

The regulatory track for Starlink reflects Baghdad’s strategy to expand advanced satellite broadband into remote, underserved, and enterprise sectors without undermining existing fiber-optic investments or state regulatory oversight.

By integrating direct licensing with legal compliance protocols, Iraqi authorities aim to regularize existing gray-market hardware, enforce data sovereignty standards, and foster competition across the telecommunications landscape.

World.title: Iran grants exceptional passage for Iraqi oil tankers via Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Following repeated formal requests submitted by the Iraqi government through multiple diplomatic and security channels, Tehran has granted exceptional transit permits for several Iraqi oil tankers, allowing them to navigate through the Strait of Hormuz amid severe maritime insecurity caused by ongoing regional conflict.

According to a report published on Saturday, August 22, 2026, by Iran’s official state news agency, IRNA, securing safe maritime passage for Iraqi crude shipments formed a core agenda item during the recent high-level visit of Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf to Baghdad.

Key Developments & Maritime Details

Exceptional Passage Clearances: Iranian maritime and military authorities approved special security permits facilitating the safe navigation of designated Iraqi crude oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz.

Persistent Diplomatic Requests: Baghdad engaged Tehran repeatedly across bilateral channels to secure formal guarantees for Iraqi energy exports traversing the vital chokepoint.

Severe Maritime Friction: Clearances were authorized despite heightened military alerts, stringent navigational restrictions, and active security threats surrounding the strategic waterway.

Bilateral Coordination: The agreement follows strategic talks in Baghdad between Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and senior Iraqi executive and security officials regarding regional stability, border coordination, and energy security.

The Strait of Hormuz remains the single most critical export conduit for southern Iraqi crude originating from the offshore terminals of Basra.

With regional maritime hostilities threatening international shipping lanes and driving up maritime insurance premiums, securing coordinated transit permits helps Baghdad maintain baseline crude export volumes and fulfill international supply commitments while pipeline diversification initiatives remain underway.

World.title: ICAR registers 16 new breeds of indigenous animals including four cattle
World.content:
Umarda, a newly registered indigenous cattle breed from Maharashtra.Â Photo Credit: ICAR-NBAGR

TOI

Newly registered indigenous livestock and dog breeds. Photo credit: ICAR-NBAGR

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Expanding the list of well-documented and scientifically recognised animal breeds in the country, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has registered 16 more new breeds of indigenous animals including cattle and buffalo, taking the total number of such breeds in India to 262. The move will help in conservation and sustainable utilisation of Indiaâs diverse and climate-resilient animal genetic resources at a time when rising temperature due to global warming is posing grave risk to animal productivity and the overall food security.The new indigenous breeds include four each of cattle (Umarda, Periyar, Koppal and Mahakaushali) and Sheep (Madgyal, Seemanchali, Kow Debar and Asomi); two goats (Totapuri and Battisi); and one each of buffalo (Gomanchali), dog (Kombai), pig (Nagal), horse/pony (Kashmiri), donkey (Braj) and yak (Sikkimese yak).These breeds, registered early this month, represent diverse agro-ecological regions spreading across 13 states -- Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra, Goa, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tamil Nadu -- and UT of Jammu & Kashmir. Goat breed Battisi is distributed across Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh whereas the sheep breed Madgyal is found in Maharashtra and Karnataka."Indigenous breeds have evolved under diverse production environments and possess locally adapted characteristics that can be valuable for climate resilience, disease adaptation, low-input production, livelihood support and sustainable livestock farming. Their conservation is therefore important not only for maintaining genetic diversity but also for ensuring the availability of adaptive livestock resources for future generations," N H Mohan, directorof the ICAR's National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR), toldKarnal-based ICAR-NBAGR is the nodal institute for registration of livestock and poultry breeds in India. With the new addition, the indigenous animal breeds now include 59 for cattle (Sahiwal, Gir, Red Kandhari and Hallikar etc.) 23 for buffalo (Murrah, Nili Ravi, Bhadawari and Mehsana etc.), 45 for goat, 50 for sheep, 16 for pigs, nine each for horses & ponies, camel and duck; five for donkey; six for dog and three for yak among others."The new registrations strengthen the national effort to reduce the proportion of nondescript livestock populations through systematic breed identification and documentation. This approach is particularly important for ensuring that valuable locally adapted populations are scientifically recognized and brought within appropriate conservation and sustainable utilization programmes," said Mohan.He said, "ICAR-NBAGR's efforts are aligned with the broader national objective of strengthening India's livestock genetic base and supporting food and nutritional security, sustainable livelihoods and climate-resilient livestock production."

World.title: Panama-flagged ship sinks off Odisha, 2 rescued; search on for 22: Shipping minister
World.content:
Two survivors have been rescued from a Panama-flagged cargo vessel that sank in the Bay of Bengal with 24 people on board, while search-and-rescue operations remain underway for the other crew members, shipping and waterways minister Sarbananda Sonowal said on Sunday.

The vessel, MV Ocean Winner, was carrying 72,100 metric tonnes of iron ore from Odisha's Paradip Port and sank about 230-240 nautical miles from the coast, according to officials and reports cited by PTI earlier. The vessel had a length overall of 225 metres and a width of 32.26 metres.

âDeeply concerned by the unfortunate incident involving MV OCEAN WINNER off the coast of Odisha. The Panama-flagged vessel was carrying iron ore from Paradip Port to China,â Sonowal said in a post on X.

âAll agencies are coordinating closely and search and rescue efforts are underway,â he said.

Sonowal added, â2 survivors have been successfully rescued and are being given medical care; their rank and identity are currently being verified.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The

(ICG) intensified its search after losing communication with the vessel on Saturday. The ship had 24 crew members, 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi national.





The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) diverted MT Aisopos, a commercial vessel in the vicinity, to assist in the search. The vessel recovered two survivors from two life rafts at about 8 pm, officials said.

The ICG had also deployed two vessels from Sri Vijaya Puram, formerly known as Port Blair, for the search-and-rescue operation, Coast Guard spokesperson Commandant Amit Uniyal said.

The vessel had left the Paradip coast at 10.42 pm on August 20, carrying iron ore fines, according to officials. An initial report by India's maritime authorities said it was bound for China, while other government information indicated Singapore as its destination.

The cause of the sinking was not immediately known.

Search operations are continuing to locate the remaining crew members, with maritime agencies coordinating efforts in the area.

World.title: 'Made-in-India chips power key space missions': IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Made-in-India semiconductor chips are powering key Indian space missions, supporting applications ranging from lunar and solar exploration to satellites and launch vehicles, Union electronics and IT minister

said on Sunday.

âMade in India chips are powering Indian Space Missions,â Vaishnaw said in a post on X on National Space Day.

According to the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY), semiconductor components designed and manufactured domestically are being used across India's space programme, strengthening the country's push for technological self-reliance.

A key contributor to this capability is the Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL) in Mohali, which develops and manufactures flight-grade semiconductor components designed to withstand the extreme conditions of space.

SCL produces specialised components, including radiation-hardened chips, electro-optical CCD and CMOS imagers, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), and sensors used to measure parameters such as pressure, acceleration, temperature and acoustics.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

These indigenous components have already been deployed in major Indian space missions, according to news agency ANI. The Chandrayaan-3 lunar lander carried an Indian-made camera chip developed by SCL Mohali for its imaging systems during the mission to the lunar surface.





India's solar mission, Aditya-L1, uses radiation-hardened analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) chips manufactured by SCL for scientific observations of the Sun.

Indigenous semiconductor technology is also being used in launch vehicles. SCL's Vikram processor is deployed in satellites and rockets, providing onboard computing capabilities required during missions.

The ministry said the growing ability to design and manufacture critical space-grade semiconductor components domestically is strengthening technological independence across India's space ecosystem.

With India planning more space missions, locally manufactured chips are expected to play an increasingly important role in supporting the country's scientific, satellite and launch infrastructure.

World.title: How Ananta Maharaj row exposed old fault lines over Netaji
World.content:
For the longest time, January 23 in 1990s Kolkata would mean small street-side political meetings where leaders of all hues would ask the youth to draw inspiration from Netaji's patriotism and ideals on his birthday.

Netaji was one of the most prominent politicians who disappeared before India became independent, and yet left a firm imprint on people's minds. The conversation around him was often about what people knew and what, they believed, had been concealed, be it the mystery surrounding his disappearance, the classified files or his political views, which parties have tried to appropriate and yet conveniently stayed away from at different times.

His own political party, the Forward Bloc, a junior partner in the long-running Left Front government in West Bengal, is now a pale shadow of its glory days. Yet Netaji remains an iconic hero not only in Bengal but across India.

Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Ray, better known as Ananta Maharaj,

for his vitriolic remarks on Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. The dust will settle soon, but what is unlikely to be ironed out any time soon is the uneasy relationship political parties in Bengal have had with the state's most enduring nationalist icon.





Ananta Maharaj rattled the hornet's nest by questioning Bose's contribution to the freedom struggle and the Indian National Army, was reported to have called him a "war criminal", and claimed the INA consisted essentially of British-Indian soldiers "captured and handed over by Germany". He also asked what the INA had achieved for Indian independence. This prompted swift action, with the Suvendu Adhikari government

, Bengal's highest civilian honour, which Mamata Banerjee's government had conferred on him.

Subsequently, Ananta apologised.

As a parting shot, the Rajya Sabha MP insisted his claims rested on material in the National Archives and invoked

over the "war criminal" description. This calls for a dispassionate look at what history actually says about these claims.

The 'war criminal' letter

Material declassified in 2016 revived a long-circulating claim that Nehru had called Bose Britain's "war criminal". The files contained a later account of an alleged Nehru dictation, not an authenticated original Nehru-to-Attlee letter.

The archival trail leads to testimony by Shyam Lal Jain, Nehru's former stenographer, who claimed decades afterwards that Nehru had dictated a December 1945 communication to British Prime Minister Clement Attlee referring to "Subhas Chandra Bose, your war criminal".

Nehru's own recorded words point in the opposite direction. On August 29, 1945, when an American journalist put it to him that Bose should be treated as a war criminal, Nehru replied: "I resent the suggestion that Subhas Bose should be dealt with as a war criminal."

In April 1956, Nehru would again write internally that "the question of War Criminals does not arise" while discussing the Netaji inquiry.

There is, however, an intriguing archival footnote. In

Conundrum

, Chandrachur Ghose and Anuj Dhar cite a 1956 Ministry of External Affairs file created after notices of parliamentary questions asking whether Bose was still regarded as a war criminal. The questions followed Forward Bloc leader Muthuramalingam Thevar's demand before the Netaji Inquiry Committee that the government clarify whether Bose's name figured on such a list.

The first response recorded in the file came from historian Sarvepalli Gopal, then head of the MEA's Historical Division. After consulting the Law and Defence ministries, Gopal wrote: "All records related to Subhas Bose were destroyed in 1947, but as far as we know Bose was not publicly designated a war criminal." The Khosla inquiry would later record an even more categorical government position: inquiries with Indian missions indicated that Bose's name had never figured on a war-criminal list.

Ghose, speaking to TOI, is equally categorical that he has found no archival evidence establishing that Bose was a war criminal. He points out, however, that such an allegation was indeed made on oath by a pendant before the Khosla Commission.

One thing, though, Ananta Maharaj does get right, Bose did not create the first INA. The INA initially took shape in Japanese-controlled Southeast Asia in 1942 under Captain Mohan Singh, built around British Indian Army soldiers who had fallen into Japanese hands during the Malaya campaign and the fall of Singapore.

It broke down amid disputes over Japanese control. Rash Behari Bose began reorganising the movement in early 1943.

Subhas Bose arrived in Southeast Asia that July and took over, after which the INA expanded dramatically in scale and political clout. So while Netaji wasn't the founder, he became the beating heart of the INA.

The BJP MP appears to have conflated two different episodes from Netaji's life in making his claim about Germany.

Before reaching Southeast Asia, Bose had run a separate military project in Germany, the Indian Legion, drawing substantially on Indian prisoners of war captured by Axis forces in North Africa.

Â Â Â Â What Nehru said on Netaji

Congress: from president to rebel

Bose's quarrel with Congress had multiple layers, some driven by the power politics of the time and others by the ideological strands to which its top leaders belonged. Bose rose to the top of the party, becoming Congress president at Haripura in 1938 and standing for a second term the following year, when he defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya, the candidate identified with Gandhi's camp, by 203 votes.

Gandhi's response became the stuff of legend: Sitaramayya's defeat, he said, was "more mine than his".

That was merely the start of the churn. Twelve of the 15 members of the Congress Working Committee resigned, the Tripuri session deepened the crisis, and Bose eventually stepped down. Nehru and Gandhi disagreed with his more confrontational line against Britain, yet Nehru was unhappy at the prospect of Bose simply being pushed out.

In April 1939, he wrote to Gandhi that doing so would be "an exceedingly wrong step".

The war drove the two much further apart. Bose read Britain's vulnerability as India's opportunity, a calculation that took him to Nazi Germany and then to Japanese-controlled Southeast Asia. Nehru fiercely opposed that route. His respect for Bose's patriotism, however, remained intact. Speaking on Bose's birthday in January 1946, he said: "I never for a moment doubted that he was a brave soldier in the struggle for freedom.

" He praised the communal unity of the INA and called the force a "legend".

Chandra Kumar Bose, Netaji's grand-nephew, makes another distinction. Recalling what his father Amiya Nath Bose, Sarat Bose's son and therefore Netaji's nephew told him, Chandra says Bose's dealings with Hitler and Tojo should not be confused with ideological admiration for either. According to him, Netaji did not like either leader; the alliances were instruments towards what he saw as the overriding objective of Indian independence.

Chandra argues that Bose's own

An Indian Pilgrim

and

The Indian Struggle

remain essential reading for anyone trying to understand his political philosophy.

The INA lost the war but gained widespread acceptance afterwards. The Red Fort trials of Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon in late 1945 produced an outpouring of public sympathy. Nehru joined their defence and donned the barrister's robes after decades away from legal practice.

Chandra also points to a famous anecdote about former British PM Clement Attlee. In a letter written two decades after their meeting, P B Chakravartti, former acting governor of West Bengal, recalled Attlee telling him during a 1956 visit that the INA's impact on the loyalty of the armed forces, followed by the Royal Indian Navy revolt, had been important in Britain's decision to leave. When asked about Gandhi's influence on the final decision, Chakravartti recalled Attlee describing it as "minimal".

From comrades to 'Fifth Column'

Before the war, Bose occupied ground that overlapped with the Indian Left. He belonged to the radical wing of nationalism and worked at building alliances with communists and other Left formations in Bengal.

The war ended that. Hitler's attack on the Soviet Union in June 1941 fundamentally changed the Communist reading of the conflict and, by the turn of 1941-42, the Communist Party had moved towards its "People's War" line.

Bose was moving in the opposite direction, towards Axis help against Britain.

P C Joshi's 1945 defence of the Communist position named the Forward Bloc, along with the Congress Socialist Party and Trotskyists, as groups that "made the Fifth Column, the agents of the Jap invader".

The original wartime publication carrying the exact words "Tojo's dog" is harder to pin down. But when CPI general secretary A B Bardhan apologised in 2010 for the party's historical assessment of Bose, contemporary reports recalled that the undivided CPI had denounced him as an "imperialist agent" and "Tojo's dog".

The rethink had started much earlier. Chandra Bose recalls Jyoti Basu publicly acknowledging the Communist misreading of Netaji. Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee followed in 2003, calling it a "great mistake" and saying,"I am apologising for our mistaken assessment of Netaji," while continuing to disagree with Bose's Axis strategy.

How INA played a key role

Samik, Forward Bloc and another old rivalry

The Ananta row was not the first this year to reopen Netaji-era wounds. In July, Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya called Forward Bloc members "goons" and alleged that they had pelted stones at Syama Prasad Mookerjee while he was addressing a gathering at Mohammed Ali Park during the 1940 Calcutta Corporation election.

He also subsequently claimed that Mookerjee had appealed to Subhas and Sarat Bose over the condition of Hindus in eastern Bengal and received no response.

Forward Bloc called

.

Ghose says the real history was more complicated. Before the 1940 Corporation election, there were negotiations for an understanding between Bose's camp and the Hindu Mahasabha. They failed. Bose's group subsequently entered into a municipal pact with the Muslim League in April 1940, a tactical arrangement that immediately became ammunition for his opponents.

Bose and Mookerjee were certainly adversaries. Mookerjee's diary records Bose warning him that if he tried to build the Hindu Mahasabha as a rival organisation in Bengal, Bose would see it broken, "by force if need be". Yet Chandrachur Ghose and Chandra Bose agree on another aspect that is often lost in today's retelling that the two remained remarkably civil towards each other despite the ideological battle.

Mookerjee had long-standing links with the Bose family, intervened with authorities over the treatment of Subhas and Sarat while they were detained, and his writings spoke of "admiration and affection" for Subhas alongside political disagreement.

Chandra adds a family footnote. After Bose's expulsion from Presidency College, Sir Asutosh Mookerjee, Syama Prasad's father, played a role in enabling him to resume his studies. Bose ultimately entered Scottish Church College.

Chandra also points to Syama Prasad's participation in Fazlul Huq's Bengal ministry. In other words, Bengal's politics in those years was full of tactical arrangements that don't align well with clean ideological lines drawn retrospectively.

Ghose goes a step further, arguing that newspapers aligned with the pro-Gandhi camp, already hostile to Bose for creating a new political organisation, also helped amplify the Bose-Mookerjee rift.

Renkoji: the argument that never ended

There is another Netaji dispute on which governments and even members of his own family have not always spoken in one voice, regarding the urn at Tokyo's Renkoji Temple, which is said to contain remains carried from Taipei following the reported plane crash of August 18, 1945.

The majority report of the Shah Nawaz Committee and the later Khosla Commission supported the plane-crash account. Prime Minister Morarji Desai told Parliament in 1978 that contradictions and later material meant their conclusions could not be treated as decisive. The Justice M K Mukherjee Commission subsequently concluded that Bose was dead but had not died in the alleged plane crash and that the Renkoji remains were not his.

Renkoji temple

Chandra Bose's own position has changed dramatically. He once questioned the crash theory, but after the declassification exercise came to the opposite conclusion. In 2024, he publicly said that the evidence from 10 national and international inquiries, taken together with the released files, convinced him that Netaji died in the August 18, 1945 crash. He now says Japan deserves credit for preserving the remains with dignity for eight decades, but that the time has come to bring them home.

Ghose, in his conversation with TOI, called for an anthropological examination of the Renkoji material, saying conventional DNA recovery may no longer be viable and insisting that any examination should be conducted under neutral observation.

From debating Bose to claiming Bose

In 2015, Mamata Banerjee's government released 64 Netaji files running to 12,744 pages and challenged the Centre to open its own records. The Modi government followed with a phased central release, beginning with 100 digitised files on January 23, 2016.

Then came the wrangling over what to call his birth anniversary. The Left had Desh Prem Divas. Mamata chose Desh Nayak Diwas. The Centre declared January 23 Parakram Diwas in 2021. In 2022, Modi unveiled Bose's statue near India Gate and said Netaji had been forgotten after Independence, his ideas and even the symbols associated with him ignored.

PM modi unveiling Netaji statue

Chandra Bose says this is precisely the problem with the politics around historical icons that their names are invoked while their ideology is often ignored. He is dismissive of Samik Bhattacharya's recent comments about Forward Bloc. Why, he asks, must one leader be pulled down simply to prop up another?

Parties of all hues have tried to appropriate different facets of Netaji's life.

The BJP has highlighted his military courage and uncompromising nationalism. The Left can point to his socialism, and anti-imperialism. Congress has the bragging rights of Netaji having been its two-time president. Ghose puts the problem another way. Bose was, as the title of his biography has it, an "inconvenient nationalist". Allegiance to the nation, he says, was the one overriding constant in Bose's politics.

That is what makes the Ananta Maharaj row worth more than a news cycle. While he lived, Bose was too difficult for any political establishment to hold comfortably. Since his disappearance, his legacy has been too valuable for any of them to concede.

World.title: Retired Hindu school teacher, wife, and children killed in Bangladesh; 2 detained
World.content:
A retired Hindu school teacher, along with his wife and two children were allegedly killed at their residence in Bangladesh’s Rangpur city, according to a media report.

The deceased were identified as Ganapati Chakraborty, 65, Pritilata Chakraborty, 50, Agami Chakraborty Prarthi, 23, and Priyam Chakraborty, 12, the Daily Star newspaper reported.

The police have detained two men, identified as Mughdho and Siddhartha, for their involvement in the killings. They are cousins.

The duo allegedly entered the rooftop of Chakraborty's house through a neighbouring building and took the drug yaba there on Thursday night (August 20, 2026), Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mohammad Abdul Mabud said in a media briefing on Sunday (August 23, 2026).

According to the official, Ganapati Chakraborty went to the rooftop after hearing noises and questioned the two men about their presence there.

To avoid being exposed, the suspects strangled him with a gamchha (thin cotton towel) he had been carrying on his shoulder, police said.

Hearing the noise, his wife went upstairs. The suspects allegedly strangled her with a piece of cloth on the staircase, the official said.

The couple's daughter and son were also killed during the incident, police said.

The bodies of the four family members were recovered from their locked house in the Daspara area of Rangpur city around 11:30 p.m. on Friday (August 21, 2026).

The police said the family had no known disputes or enmity with anyone.

World.title: No new H1N1 strain in India, existing vaccines sufficient, says ICMR
World.content:
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) on Sunday (August 23, 2026) said that the Influenza A (H1N1) viruses currently circulating in the country belong to the A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like virus strain. It clarified that no new strain of H1N1 has been identified and there is no cause for panic.

“These viruses belong to clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1, and have been in circulation since 2025. The Influenza strains currently circulating are also well matched with the vaccine strains recommended for the Northern Hemisphere,” ICMR said. “Seasonal influenza, including H1N1, is mostly self-limiting,” it added.

Common symptoms of the illness include fever, cough, headache, and body ache, and most people recover with appropriate care and rest. However, young children, elderly persons, and individuals with underlying medical conditions may be at a greater risk of complications. If symptoms persist, worsen, or become severe, consultation with a doctor is advised, it said.

The Union Health Ministry has said that it is closely monitoring the situation through regular surveillance and is undertaking necessary public health measures.

India has registered a rise in seasonal Influenza A(H1N1) cases, commonly called swine flu, this monsoon, especially in major cities. Delhi has reported 1,777 confirmed H1N1 cases so far this year, including 114 new cases on August 20. Karnataka has registered over 4,000 cases, with more than half reported from Bengaluru. Rising influenza activity has also been reported in Mumbai, Chennai and parts of Kerala.

National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) data show that H1N1 activity was relatively low in 2021 (778 cases, 12 deaths) after the pandemic period, but rebounded sharply in 2022 (13,202 cases, 410 deaths) and remained substantial in 2023 (8,125 cases, 129 deaths). By June 2024, India had already recorded 7,215 cases and 150 deaths, and year-end numbers were higher. NCDC’s 2025 reporting shows that H1N1 continued to circulate across multiple States.

NCDC maintains a nationwide influenza surveillance network and publishes State-wise data and H1N1 treatment/prevention guidelines. It recommends seasonal influenza vaccination based on WHO strain recommendations. For the 2025–26 season, India’s recommended trivalent vaccine included H1N1, H3N2 and B/Victoria components, with circulating Indian H1N1 strains aligning with vaccine strains.

“People at higher risk should consider annual vaccination and seek medical advice promptly if flu symptoms become severe,” Anil Bansal of the Delhi Medical Association said.

World.title: Two drown in sea, two rescued at Kakinada
World.content:
Two persons drowned in the sea at Kakinada beach on Sunday, while two others were rescued by visitors. All four are residents of Kakinada.

According to an official release issued by Kakinada police, A. Sri Ganesh Chanti, 21, and 19-year-old K.A.V. Sandeep Kumar were rescued by beachgoers. The incident occurred when the group of four friends were bathing in the sea.

A search operation has been launched to trace Padala Yuva Kishore, 20, and 21-year-old Anusuri Veerababu.

World.title: BJP is wasting time over unnecessary issues, says Laxman Savadi
World.content:
BJP leaders are deliberately disrupting the Assembly proceedings and wasting precious time and public resources over unnecessary issues, Minister Laxman Savadi said in Vijayapura on Sunday.

It is the BJP that said that it will conduct a crop loss study before the Session. Its leaders went on talking about a drought impact study. They said that they will submit a report to the State government. But it is the same BJP that is wasting the time of the House now, the Cooperation Minister said.

He said that the continued disruption of the House is meaningless as there is no time for discussions on relevant issues.

“In the first week of the Session, they spent talking about one person. They are not behaving as a responsible Opposition party. BJP leaders, who only make accusations, do not seem to have the courage to speak. We have told them many times to present facts with relevant evidence. But they do not want to follow the sacred Parliamentary traditions. They only want to attack the Minister and defame him. The Lokayukta has already cleared B. Nagendra of the said charge. If the BJP leaders have any more information, they should present them properly. I pray that God gives them the wisdom to talk about relevant subjects like reduced rainfall and drought impact and the Union government’s assistance in calamity relief to the State,” he said.

“There are drought conditions prevailing in the State and surveys by the Agriculture, Horticulture and Revenue departments are under way. Once these departments submit their reports, the Chief Minister will discuss with Ministers concerned and officers and the Cabinet will decide on the issue of loan waiver. There has been a demand for cloud seeding for a long time and the Chief Minister will take the final decision,” he said.

“I have been in different parties in my 25 years of public life. But my politics has been secular. The Congress recognized me and gave me the responsibility of being the Cooperation Minister. I plan to strengthen the department. Though the Union government has created a Ministry for Cooperation, it has not introduced any special schemes or projects. We will work with the existing projects,” he said in response to a query.

World.title: With new stores, U.P. aims to integrate khadi with employment
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh government on Sunday (August 23, 2026) said it would launch new khadi outlets across the State to boost sales among youth, and integrate khadi with employment.

“Preparations are underway to open new Khadi stores in the State. In a recent meeting, the Minister of Khadi and Village Industries, Silk, Handloom and Textiles, has directed the opening of new khadi stores in locations with a strong base of customers, after surveying all sales centres, training institutes, and assets. The department’s push is for increased availability of khadi products in universities, technical institutions, medical colleges, and public places, with special attention given to the branding, promotion, and marketing of khadi products,” a statement from the government said.

In a recent meeting held at the Khadi Bhavan in Dalibagh, Lucknow, the government highlighted its focus on village industries in khadi, handloom, and silk sectors for the rural economy, and generation of employment.

“The benefits of schemes should reach eligible beneficiaries on time, and 100% of the budget should be utilised. Targets for all schemes, including the Chief Minister’s Village Industries Employment Scheme and the Pandit Deendayal Village Industries Development Assistance Scheme, along with quality improvement and skill training, should be met within specified time limits. Pending cases should be resolved promptly at the bank level, and loans should be made available to eligible beneficiaries. All training centres should be equipped with modern facilities, and development work should be completed,” senior government officials told the representatives of banks.

The Uttar Pradesh Khadi and Village Industries Board is also aiming to complete the construction of a common facilities centre in Kushinagar. “Extensive publicity will be ensured for upcoming Khadi exhibitions and festivals on various platforms,” the statement said.

World.title: KTR calls for State-wide protests from September 2 on ‘govt. failures’
World.content:
Hyderabad

The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) will launch a major campaign State-wide to expose the “Congress government’s betrayal of people as it completes 1,000 days in office”.

The party will organise a series of innovative programmes across Telangana for a week from September 2, highlighting the alleged failure of the Congress government to fulfil its promises.

BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao directed senior party leaders, elected representatives and the State committee, during a teleconference on Sunday, and called upon them to take the ‘failures’ to every section of people across the State.

KTR said that the Congress came to power after making numerous promises to people, including the 420 vows, 13 declarations and six guarantees, assuring them that these commitments would be implemented within 100 days. However, even after 1,000 days in office, it had failed to fully fulfil even a single promise, he alleged.

The programmes from September 2 should not be confined merely to the promises made by Congress. These should also highlight the failures of the government after it assumed office and the problems currently being faced by different sections of society.

Mr. Rama Rao said that the ‘failure’ of the Congress government to clear more than ₹12,000 crore in fee reimbursement dues, should be highlighted among students and their parents across colleges. He recalled that BRS had already exposed the alleged betrayal of the youth through the meeting held in Saroornagar and the Yuva Sangrama Sadassu.

KTR also suggested that different programmes be conducted over the seven-day period, with party leaders meeting women, farmers, youth, students, Dalits, BCs, tribals and other sections in the constituencies.

World.title: Iran says new sanctions threatened by ‘desperate’ U.S. will fail
World.content:
Iran’sForeign Minister dismissed the threat of ‌new U.S. sanctions as a sign of desperation on Sunday (August 23, 2026) and said the expected new ​measures would fail to defeat Tehran.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is due to ⁠hold a press conference at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday (August 24, 2026), has threatened to impose “the toughest sanctions in history” on Iran.

Iran’s economy is already under huge pressure from international sanctions, its infrastructure has been hit repeatedly and thousands of people have been killed ‌in airstrikes on the Islamic Republic since the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on February 28.

But Tehran remains defiant after nearly six months of war and has brought shipping to a virtual ‌standstill in the Strait of Hormuz, refusing to allow unauthorized oil tankers to transit a waterway that ‌is ⁠vital for global oil shipments. The effective blockade of the strait has pushed up global ⁠oil prices.

Describing what he said were “repetitive scenarios”, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a video posted on Telegram: “The fact that they [U.S. leaders] have moved on from military operations ... to bring up the same old plans shows that they are desperate.”

He said Washington must speak to ​Iran respectfully to find “a solution based on ‌justice and honour.”

“We have never been afraid. All of their actions — whether blockades or other military moves they have made — have failed, and this new issue of theirs will fail as well,” he said.

U.S. President Donald Trump has warned of economic consequences against any country that provides “any type of lifeline to Iran,” ‌and Mr. Bessent has urged cooperation with Washington by China, which buys more than 80% of Iran’s ​shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler. China has urged diplomacy.

PAKISTAN’S ARMY CHIEF TO VISIT TEHRAN

Iran said Pakistan’s army chief, Asim Munir, would visit Tehran on Monday (August 24, 2026) ⁠as part of efforts to restore peace and security in the region, but gave few details.

Pakistan has been mediating in the conflict and a Pakistani government source said Mr. Munir would touch on recent developments including the U.S. threat ‌of new sanctions.

Mr. Trump said on Friday (August 21) that Washington was observing “what happens” in the conflict.

“They would love to make a deal, but they’re not ready to make the right deal, in my opinion,” Mr. Trump said of Iran.

U.S. attacks have severely diminished Iran’s economy and devastated its navy and air force, but Tehran maintains enough missile and drone capability to impede oil tanker traffic and attack regional rivals.

Iranian Parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said on Saturday (August 22) that Tehran had received “numerous messages” from neighbouring countries about establishing new regional security arrangements and economic cooperation.

Mr. Qalibaf did not ‌say which countries he was referring to. He accused the U.S. of endangering the security of its allies in the region for ​the sake of Israel, adding that an independent, “homegrown” regional order would deliver peace and security.

Mr. Trump has yet to achieve objectives he set at the start of the war, such ⁠as dismantling Iran’s nuclear programme — the state of which remains uncertain given that U.N. inspectors have been shut out since ⁠2025 — and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers.

While Iran remains defiant, President Masoud Pezeshkian has also called for a diplomatic solution.

“It would be better to end the war today, when ‌we are powerful and have dignity, and the whole world acknowledges our victory and emphasizes that America, contrary to all regulations, attacked our schools, hospitals, and infrastructure and is hated in the world,” the ISNA news ​agency quoted him as saying on Friday (August 21).

World.title: PMK urges T.N. govt. to sue Karnataka for ₹1,000 crore in compensation over water-sharing disputes
World.content:
PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss has urged the Tamil Nadu Government to sue Karnataka for ₹1,000 crore in compensation over water-sharing disputes affecting farmers.

At a party function held in Salem on Sunday (August 23, 2026), Dr. Anbumani said that the Karnataka’s ‘failure’ to release Cauvery water had severely affected Kuruvai cultivation in Tamil Nadu. Until now two lakh acres in the Delta region have had no water for irrigation. The super El Nino effect had disrupted the southwest monsoon, reducing the chances of rain till November. Therefore, Samba cultivation is likely to be affected as well. While there is 90% water in Karnataka’s dams, that state refuses to share water. Following heavy rain in Wayanad, Kabini dam receives water and the surplus water is discharged to Tamil Nadu. The Tamil Nadu government should fight to get its share of water from Karnataka.

Demanding an all-party meeting on the proposed Mekedatu project, Dr. Anbumani said Karnataka had said it would only use 5 tmc for the drinking water needs of Bengaluru, and leave the rest for Tamil Nadu. Would Karnataka agree if Tamil Nadu were to construct a dam and provide water to Bengaluru?

On caste census, Dr. Anbumani said that PMK founder S. Ramadoss had met with former Chief Ministers including M.G. Ramachandran, M. Karunanidhi, Edappadi K. Palaniswami and M.K. Stalin regarding the issue. But, they did not do anything. “After the TVK government came to power, I met with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in this regard and the government accepted the demand of the caste census. Now the announcement has come and the PMK will push for its implementation,” he said.

World.title: PTI demands Imran's CT angiography be conducted at Shifa International Hospital
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Following reports that jailed PTI founder Imran Khan could not undergo a recommended computed tomography angiography (CTA) during a hospital visit this week, his party condemned the authorities over their “continued failure” to carry out the procedure and demanded that it be immediately conducted at Shifa International Hospital.

When the PTI founder was brought to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) in the early hours of Friday for an eye procedure and other diagnostic examinations, doctors recommended a CTA of the heart, but hospital staff reportedly said the facility was unavailable. After other tests, he was subsequen­tly shifted back to Adiala jail, reportedly without under­going the CTA, which can help identify coronary blo­ckages and assess the risk of a heart attack.

Sources told Dawn the Cardiac Centre’s conventional angiography facility at Pims was different from CTA. While conventional angiography involves inserting a catheter into a blood vessel, CTA is performed using a CT scanner and does not require puncturing a vein.

Doctors pointed out that a 128-slice CT scanner had been operational in Pims’ radiology department since March 2022 and was capable of performing CTA. The test is generally conducted by radiologists on the recommendation of clinicians. A senior doctor said the patient should therefore have been referred to radiology department.

Taking notice of the reports, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday formed an inquiry committee, headed by the establishment division secretary, to establish facts and fix responsibility.

On Sunday, PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram, in a written message to Dawn, reiterated the PTI’s demand to move Imran to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad without any delay — which the Supreme Court had also directed on August 18.

Akram also cited details submitted to the court, saying a medical board of the government had examined Imran on August 10 while a Pims cardiologist had already recommended CT Coronary Angiography for him on August 1 due to fluctuating blood pressure, palpitations, headaches, restlessness and the potential risk of cardiac complications arising from his age and prolonged isolation.

“Even the government’s own doctors considered this diagnostic test necessary,” Akram stated. “Yet, when Imran Khan was taken to Pims, the procedure was not performed. Hospital officials claimed that the required facility was unavailable, despite the presence of a functional CT scanner in the radiology department capable of conducting the test,” he alleged.

He said these reports had “intensified concerns regarding repeated delays and apparent negligence in providing Imran Khan with timely and appropriate medical care”.

“A former prime minister was taken to a government hospital in the middle of the night, assessed by doctors who recommended an essential cardiac investigation, and then returned to the Adiala jail without the test being conducted. This cannot be dismissed as an isolated administrative lapse; it reflects a deeply troubling pattern,” he added.

Akram said, on the other hand, the required facilities were available at Shifa International Hospital. “But, despite the Supreme Court’s order concerning Imran Khan’s comprehensive medical examination and treatment at Shifa International, the authorities chose not to take him there and instead transferred him to a facility where the CT Coronary Angiography was ultimately not conducted,” he rued.

“When the necessary facilities were available at Shifa International, deliberately taking Imran Khan to a hospital where the required facilities for the procedure were not available raises a grave and unavoidable question: was the decision made in advance to prevent the CTA from being conducted?” he asked. “The authorities must explain why he was not taken to the facility specifically identified for his medical care and why he was sent to a hospital where the recommended test could not be performed.”

Akram rejected the government’s assertions that Imran had been receiving adequate medical care.

Regarding the prime minister’s decision to constitute an inquiry committee following reports of the failure to conduct Imran’s CTA, he said the move raised “serious questions as to why the medically recommended test was not conducted in the first instance. Why coordination between the cardiology and radiology departments had failed, and why Imran Khan was not taken to Shifa International despite the availability of the required facilities there”.

He demanded that Imran’s CTA be immediately conducted at Shifa International Hospital under the supervision of independent specialists and the former premier’s personal physicians.

Akram also called for the “prompt disclosure of his (Imran’s) complete medical records, reports and diagnostic results to his family, personal doctors and legal team”.

Moreover, the Supreme Court’s August 18 decision should be fully implemented in letter and spirit and a transparent and independent investigation should be conducted to determine why Imran was taken to Pims instead of Shifa International and why his CTA was not conducted, Akram demanded.

“Imran Khan’s heart health cannot be subjected to political calculations, administrative excuses or further delay,” Akram declared.

“Political victimisation must never be permitted to endanger a human life through the denial or postponement of essential medical care. The decision to take him to a facility where the required test was not conducted, despite the availability of the necessary facilities at Shifa International, has created serious concerns that the procedure was intentionally prevented,” he alleged. “The government and all relevant authorities will bear full responsibility for any further deterioration in his condition,” Akram warned.

Imran’s hospital transfer saga

The PTI has been raising concerns over Imran’s health since his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January. He has been taken to Pims multiple times for treatment since.

On Tuesday, the Supreme Court ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board.

A three-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and comprising Justices Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibr­ahim issued the interim directions on petitions seeking Imran’s hospitalisation, access to personal physicians and family members and provision of his medical record to his family.

The court also ordered that Dr Uzma Khan and Dr Faisal Sultan — Imran Khan’s personal physician — be present during the medical check-up by a medical board.

At the same time, Imran’s family members, PTI members and lawyers associated with him were barred from disclosing his health condition or medical reports to the media or public until the next hearing.

The next day, the government filed a review plea against the court’s order to shift Imran to the private hospital, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice.

However, the SC had returned the plea on Thursday with the objection that the contents of the affidavit and facts, along with the review petition filed under Article 188 of the Constitution, had not been properly drawn up and that one of the paper books was not in order.

The same night, elaborate arrangements were put in place in and around Shifa International Hospital, and all signs pointed to the PTI founder being brought there, in compliance with the Supreme Court order.

However, it became clear on Friday morning that Imran had been taken to Pims for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside Al Shifa Hospital” for the diversion.

In a post on X, he said, “In the light of the SC’s order, the prisoner was taken to the hospital under appropriate security arrangements during the night between August 20 and 21.

“A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist, and a physician, conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit,” he said.

The PTI rejected the allegation and flayed the government for “flouting” the SC order.

Later, the Pims administration said that two specialists from Shifa Inter­national Hospital participated in Imran’s eye assessment, while other exa­minations were carri­­ed out by the concerned Pims specialists.

“The clinical input ari­sing from the ophthalmological assessment was taken into account alongside findings of the investigations conducted at Pims,” the statement said.

World.title: Sindh govt to seek judicial commission to review Mir Raza Ali murder probe; family to move SHC against decision
World.content:
The Sindh government said on Sunday it would be asking the chief justice of the provincial high court to establish a judicial commission to determine whether the investigation in the Mir Raza Ali murder case was being conducted impartially and in accordance with the law.

But, soon after the announcement, the counsel for Ali’s family raised objections and said they would approach the Sindh High Court on Monday against the decision.

The Sindh government’s decision came days after Ali’s parents approached Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, requesting that he directly supervise the investigation.

His parents, Mir Hussain and Mariam, wrote a letter to the Sindh chief minister through their lawyer Jibran Nasir, alleging that the investigation continued to suffer as the probe team “appears to focus on perpetuating the false narrative of the death of the deceased by suicide”.

A statement issued by the Sindh chief minister’s office on Sunday said their letter had been received with “compassion and the utmost seriousness”.

“After carefully considering the concerns expressed by the family, the government of Sindh has decided to request the honourable chief justice of the Sindh High Court to establish a judicial commission to conduct an impartial and transparent inquiry,” the statement said.

It added that the commission should determine whether the investigation in the case was being conducted impartially and in accordance with law. It should also identify any investigative angle or evidence requiring further investigation.

Moreover, the commission should determine whether “any police officer, medico-legal officer or other official committed negligence, dereliction of duty, professional misconduct, suppression or manipulation of evidence, or any unlawful act, omission or cover-up”.

The commission may recommend further investigation, forensic analysis and appropriate legal or departmental action wherever warranted, the statement said.

“For the effective discharge of its mandate, the commission shall exercise all powers available to it under the Sindh Tribunals of Inquiry Ordinance, 1969, including the powers of a civil court to summon and enforce the attendance of witnesses, examine them on oath, and require the discovery and production of documents and other records.

“All government departments, agencies and officials have been directed to extend full cooperation to the commission and provide every record, document and form of assistance sought by it. The Home Department shall provide the necessary secretariat support,” the statement read.

It added that the commission should submit its report, together with its findings and recommendations, to the Sindh government within 30 days of its constitution, or within such extended period as may be allowed where necessary for a complete and fair inquiry.

“The commission will be fully empowered to examine the conduct of the investigation and recommend appropriate action in accordance with law,” it said.

The government also expressed solidarity with Ali’s family in this time of grief.

Reacting to the provincial government’s decision, counsel for Ali’s family, Jibran Nasir, posted on X that they would move the Sindh High Court tomorrow to form a joint investigation team (JIT) and oppose the planned commission.

“Forming a judicial commission without informing the family of Mir Raza, nor making the terms of reference of the inquiry public. Why are other law enforcement agencies not engaged and a JIT [is not] formed? Why is the criminal conduct of police officers not investigated? Tomorrow, the family will move the high court for JIT and to oppose the judicial commission,” he wrote on X.

He pointed out that police were yet to submit an investigation report before the magistrate. “Before the submission of the police report, why has the Sindh govt announced a judicial commission? Is it because they know the outcome of the police investigation and they disagree with it?” he questioned.

The case

Ali, a 25-year-old businessman and a graduate of the Institute of Business Administration, was found dead with a gunshot wound on July 29 in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar a day after he was reported missing.

While his family was convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police were initially building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

A murder charge was eventually added to the first information report (FIR) after the exhumation and a second post-mortem of Ali’s body revealed that he had suffered multiple injuries and was shot in the back, ruling out the possibility of suicide.

The second autopsy was conducted after a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination.

On August 6, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Ali’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with police surgeon Dr Sumaiyya Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed.

But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, the counsel for Ali’s family, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on August 8.

A day later, the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death while Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan transferred the investigation into Ali’s murder to Zaman Town police station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was registered.

The same day, the Sindh government decided to seek a judicial commission for the case’s investigation, only to defer the plan a day later after Ali’s family said they had made no such demand and had faith in the new investigation team.

Letter to CM

But on Wednesday, they wrote to the Sindh chief minister, expressing dissatisfaction with the probe.

In their 22-page letter to Murad, which went into extensive detail about the incident and subsequent investigations, as well as the controversies surrounding the case, they stated that the “murderers and the conspirators of murder… despite public scrutiny continue to appear to exercise considerable political clout to ensure that the truth remains suppressed”.

The letter said that Raza’s parents “are horrified at the level of corruption, incompetence and political influence prevalent within Sindh Police”.

In the letter, Advocate Nasir, on behalf of the victim’s family, demanded the immediate suspension of police officers who were part of the original investigation team.

Referring to Sindh police’s statement on Tuesday that it had ruled out suicide following the second post-mortem examination of the body, the letter questioned “why the current investigation team continues to spend time and energy analysing and re-analysing these reports rather than focusing on securing and rationalising multiple other sources of evidence”.

The letter then listed 24 questions that remained unanswered in the investigation, including those concerning Raza’s communications shortly before his murder and the circumstances surrounding his death. It also raised questions about missing digital and forensic evidence.

The letter further pointed out that police had not answered questions concerning the alleged actions of Raza’s business partner in the days immediately before and after his murder.

“The police hierarchy has been reduced to a tool used to corrupt and later destroy the crime scene,” the letter alleged.

The previous investigation team’s conduct “attracts multiple penal offences under the Pakistan Penal Code”, the letter said, specifically mentioning Section 201, for “causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender”, and Section 218, relating to a “public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent” to save someone from punishment.

The letter went on to propose 10 charges against the police officers concerned, including deliberate mishandling of material evidence, failure to record witness statements, deliberate manipulation of the investigation record, unlawful handling of the deceased’s devices, and “abuse of official position and concerted acts to defeat the course of investigation”, among others.

The letter also proposed 13 terms of reference for a departmental inquiry against the police officers, including an inquiry into “why the former investigation team prematurely adopted and promoted the theory of suicide” and “why the investigation team failed to respond to and heed the letter of the Police Surgeon Karachi”.

The letter also questioned why the special medical board had faced resistance and called for an examination into “the custody, handling and forensic examination of the deceased’s smartwatch”.

It further urged the departmental inquiry to “determine whether any senior police officer, public office-holder or other person improperly influenced, directed or pressured the former investigation team to adopt, maintain or promote the suicide narrative or otherwise interfere with the investigation”.

World.title: Hina Javed murder case: Rawalpindi court sends husband, servant on 3-day physical remand
World.content:
RAWALPINDI: A duty magistrate in Rawalpindi on Sunday remanded the husband and servant of Hina Javed in police custody for three days in her murder case.

Hina was found dead in the washroom of her apartment in Askari Apartments in Rawalpindi on Thursday evening. Police said that the body bore signs of torture, with a wire fastened around her neck and tied to the shower rod. They detained her husband and a servant in relation to the case.

Today, the suspects were produced before a duty magistrate by police, who sought their remand for further investigation.

The court granted the Civil Lines police their three-day physical remand, directing authorities to submit a progress report after the remand’s completion.

The FIR

A first information report of the case was registered on Aug 20 at the Civil Lines police station under Sections 302 (premeditated murder) and 34 (common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The complainant, Hina’s brother, Fahid Javed, alleged in the FIR that his sister had been murdered by her husband, her father-in-law and their domestic servant.

Fahid told police that he received a telephone call from his sister’s father-in-law at 6:53pm on Thursday, informing him of an emergency at their residence. He said he rushed to the apartment with other family members and arrived there at 7:23pm.

He claimed that when he arrived at the residence, he found his sister’s body in the bathroom.

The complainant further alleged that his sister had been subjected to “severe torture and mistreatment” by her husband. He also claimed that she might have been administered a poisonous substance before her death.

In his complaint, Fahid said Hina had married the suspect in November 2025.

An initial postmortem examination indicated a strangulation mark around her neck, an injury below her right lip and bleeding.

On Sunday, police sources told Dawn the cause of death could be ascertained with finality after the Punjab Forensic Science Agency’s (PFSA) report was received.

The sources said the role of Hina’s father-in-law in the case was also yet to be determined and that he was being questioned and asked not to leave the city.

Meanwhile, they added, a seven-member team, headed by Rawalpindi Senior Superintendent of Police (Investigation) Saifullah had been formed to investigate the case.

The sources also said that mobile phones of the victim and three of her family members had been taken into custody for investigation.

World.title: Cricket greats appeal to PM Shehbaz for Imran's treatment in line with Supreme Court directives
World.content:
Twenty-two international cricketers, including 21 ex-captains, have written a letter to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, making an appeal for ex-Pakistani premier Imran Khan’s medical treatment in line with recent Supreme Court directives, ESPN Cricinfo reported on Sunday.

On August 18, the Supreme Court directed the government to move Imran to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital, a private facility, within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board.

However, it later turned out that Imran was instead taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims).

Meanwhile, it was also reported that he could not undergo a recommended computed tomography angiography (CTA) at Pims as the required facilities were unavailable at the hospital.

The letter written by the 22 ex-cricketers and cited by ESPN Cricinfo stated: “Pakistan’s Supreme Court ordered that Imran Khan be transferred to hospital for examination by a medical board that was to include his own personal physicians and his sister, Dr Uzma Khan.

“The court also reinstated weekly family visits. These were very welcome steps.”

However, the former cricketers noted, Imran’s hospital stay lasted only a few hours.

“He was examined by a state-appointed team rather than the board the court had directed, declared ‘medically fit’, and returned to Adiala Jail before that board could complete its work,” the letter claimed, according to ESPN Cricinfo.

The former cricketers called for:

Permitting the medical board directed by the Supreme Court — including Imran’s own doctors — to complete a full and independent assessment of his health, particularly the reported loss of vision in his right eye.

Honouring the weekly family visits reinstated by the court without interruption or administrative delay

Providing the recommended treatment to Imran without delay following the outcome of his medical assessment

The letter’s signatories included Michael Atherton, Alex Blackwell, Allan Border, Michael Brearley, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Alastair Cook, Michael Gatting, Sunil Gavaskar, Lee Germon, Adam Gilchrist, David Gower, Kim Hughes, Nasser Hussain, Clive Lloyd, Kapil Dev, Arjuna Ranatunga, Andrew Strauss, Dilip Vengsarkar, Steve Waugh and John Wright.

In their appeal, they said they were writing “not as politicians, but as former colleagues and rivals who share a bond forged on the cricket field“ and that they did not seek to adjudicate Pakistan’s domestic legal processes.
