During a transitional period, neutral packaging in English or Russian, or rebranding, could potentially be used. The appearance of Azerbaijani fuel on the Armenian market has already created a precedent for a kind of “economic truce”. A similarly pragmatic approach could work in the opposite direction, although this will not happen automatically.

In both societies, support for peace does not yet necessarily translate into an equally positive attitude towards goods from the neighbouring country. Traders from border areas who wished to remain anonymous, as well as entrepreneurs with experience of informal “re-exports” through Georgia using channels that have existed since the 1990s, say that price and quality could eventually become the decisive factors. However, this process could take years.

Practical obstacles and possible timeframes

Issues surrounding certification, phytosanitary controls, customs procedures, bank transfers and insurance have yet to be fully resolved.

Logistics currently operate mainly through Georgia. Direct rail links and the TRIPP corridor are still at the infrastructure development stage. Competition also remains high, with suppliers from Turkey, Russia and Iran already present in the market alongside domestic producers. The competitiveness of Armenian goods will therefore depend on their price, quality and logistics costs.

Under an optimistic scenario, small-scale shipments of industrial goods and raw materials could begin within several months to a year. A more realistic scenario would see trade gradually expand over one to three years, while under a pessimistic scenario, political fluctuations and public reaction could delay the process considerably.

What to watch next

Key indicators could include the first genuine commercial shipments from Armenia appearing in customs statistics, the introduction of banking mechanisms for cross-border payments, official approval of a list of potential goods for trade, and changes in the procurement policies of retailers such as Bravo, Araz and others.

Independent polling and sociological research in both countries will also be needed to assess public attitudes towards goods labelled “Made in …”. Without such data, statements about future trade will remain largely expressions of intent.

World.title: ‘From crisis management to stability’: Pashinyan unveils new government programme
World.content:
Armenia’s 2026–2031 government programme

The Armenian government has approved its programme for 2026-2031. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said it marked a shift from crisis management to stability. Looking back on his eight years as prime minister, he said the coronavirus pandemic, followed by the war and the post-war situation, had forced the government to operate in crisis-management mode. Now that Armenia and Azerbaijan have established peace, the government can “return to the unfinished part of the agenda of the 2018 Velvet Revolution”.

The new programme focuses on stability, he said. Pashinyan stressed that it rests entirely on the concept of “Real Armenia” and the principles underpinning the establishment of the Fourth Republic.

In 2025, the ruling Civil Contract party announced a new strategic goal: establishing the Fourth Republic of Armenia. The party congress unanimously adopted a declaration to this effect. According to the document, the Fourth Republic “will be based on the concept of preserving the internationally recognised sovereign territory of the Republic of Armenia, covering 29,743 sq km, in accordance with the 1991 Alma-Ata Declaration”. The declaration says the party reached this decision after analysing the history of the Third Republic. The Third Republic refers to the present-day Republic of Armenia, which declared independence following a nationwide referendum in 1991. The First Republic refers to the republic proclaimed on 28 May 1918. Accordingly, Soviet Armenia is considered the Second Republic.

“Following the 7 June 2026 election, the ideology of ‘Real Armenia’ won. This means it has become the official ideology. Armenia is therefore entering the stage of its history that we call the Fourth Republic. We must continue and give new momentum to democratic, anti-corruption, economic and public administration reforms,” the prime minister stressed.

Government plans for the next five years

According to the new programme, the Armenian government will pursue the following goals in 2026-2031:

strengthening and further institutionalising the peace established between Armenia and Azerbaijan;

maintaining and further developing a favourable security environment around Armenia, in particular by normalising and developing relations with countries in the region and deepening existing partnerships beyond it;

unblocking Armenia through the Crossroads of Peace project and the “Trump Route” (TRIPP) transit programme;

liberalising the visa regime with the EU for Armenian citizens;

deepening democratic, anti-corruption, economic and public administration reforms.

With whom does Yerevan plan to deepen partnerships under its “balanced foreign policy”?

In 2026-2031, the Armenian government will pursue a “balanced and proportionate” foreign policy.

“It has proved effective in stabilising Armenia’s external environment. Regionalisation plays a key role in foreign policy, whose goal is to ensure conditions in which Armenia can not only live without external support, but do so comfortably,” the document says.

Based on this approach, the government places particular importance on further developing relations with Georgia, Iran, Turkey and Azerbaijan. The government has outlined the following steps for each neighbouring country:

Georgia

Yerevan will continue implementing the measures set out in the Declaration on Establishing a Strategic Partnership between Armenia and Georgia. This will create new mutually beneficial opportunities for political, trade, economic, energy and transport cooperation, as well as regional and joint infrastructure projects.

Iran

Armenia will continue energy cooperation with Iran, develop cross-border infrastructure and expand transport routes through Iran, including North-South and Persian Gulf-Black Sea corridors.

Turkey

The Armenian government will continue efforts to establish diplomatic relations with Turkey, open the Armenian-Turkish border and put at least two modern border crossing points into operation. It also plans to restore and expand transport, energy and digital infrastructure, as well as bilateral and multilateral trade.

Azerbaijan

The government plans to continue efforts to sign and ratify a peace agreement and carry out work on the delimitation and demarcation of the state border. Contacts between civil society and business communities in the two countries will continue, helping to establish bilateral trade.

The foreign policy priorities specifically include deepening strategic partnerships with the European Union, the US, France and China. With Russia, Armenia plans to “transform and deepen its partnership”.

Against the backdrop of tensions over the ban on Armenian food and other exports to Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), which Russia leads, the programme says:

“Work will continue to ensure the full and uninterrupted exercise of the EAEU’s fundamental freedoms — the free movement of labour, services, goods and capital — as well as to develop relations with member and observer states.”

Regarding relations with the European Union, the programme stresses that Armenia will continue working to meet standards in democracy and the rule of law, as well as in the economic, financial and other spheres.

Armenia intends to deepen its partnership with the United States further. Cooperation will continue based on the principles set out in the Strategic Partnership Charter and bilateral memorandums of understanding.

“The TRIPP project, the ‘Trump Route’, will be implemented, at least in terms of operating energy and railway infrastructure, while integrating Armenia into major regional infrastructure projects,” the programme says.

Armenia’s 2026–2031 government programme

World.title: Parrots Rocky and Kiki: Tbilisi Zoo’s brightest residents – video
World.content:
Macaws at Tbilisi Zoo

Tbilisi Zoo is home to two species of macaws: scarlet macaws (Ara macao) named Rocky and Kiki, and blue-and-yellow macaws (Ara ararauna) named Chico and Paco. Their bright plumage catches visitors’ attention at first sight.

The macaws at Tbilisi Zoo are currently in the middle of their breeding season. Chico and Paco are expecting chicks. They usually incubate their eggs for 24–28 days. During this period, both parents actively protect and care for their future offspring.

Rocky and Kiki have become particularly cautious during this period. They often hide from people and rarely leave their enclosure. If you are planning to visit them at the zoo, keep in mind that they may be difficult to spot at the moment.

Macaws are known for their strong bonds. Pairs almost always stay together: they preen each other’s feathers, look for food together and protect each other when danger threatens.

With proper care, macaws can live for 50–60 years, and sometimes even longer — more than 70 years. Rocky’s exact age is unknown, but he is the oldest parrot at Tbilisi Zoo. Despite his advanced age, Rocky still has the same short-tempered and grumpy nature he has always had.

Once, when a keeper was a little late with a treat — a nut — Rocky immediately made his “protest” known by biting him on the finger. Because of their powerful beaks, macaw bites can be very painful and may cause serious injuries.

Macaws are incredibly intelligent birds. They have excellent memories, and some can even imitate human voices and words.

Although macaws are often kept as pets, caring for them is no easy task. They need plenty of space, daily attention, mental stimulation and constant variety in their surroundings.

Tbilisi Zoo‘s history spans nearly a century. It was founded on 10 February 1927 on the basis of the Caucasian Society for the Acclimatisation of Animals, which had been keeping wild animals since the early 20th century, though without official zoo status. The zoo was originally built on 70 hectares in the Vere River gorge. Over the years, the expansion of the capital — and later the devastating flood of 13 June 2015 — significantly reduced the territory of the old zoo. Today, it covers five hectares and is home to around 1,500 animals, each with its own story. In this video series, we will introduce you to the residents of Tbilisi Zoo. We will show how their day unfolds, how they interact with other animals and people, and how their behaviour changes depending on the weather and the season. Get ready to hear many fascinating stories.

Macaws at Tbilisi Zoo

World.title: Opinion from Abkhazia: ‘Nika Gvaramia said nothing new about resolving Georgian-Abkhaz conflict’
World.content:
An interview with Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Georgian opposition, about ways to resolve the Georgian-Abkhaz conflict attracted considerable attention in Georgia. In Abkhazia, however, it attracted almost no attention.

In his blog, Inal Khashig, editor of the Abkhaz newspaper Chegemskaya Pravda, offered his view on why. He believes the lack of interest among Abkhaz people is mainly because Gvaramia said nothing new in the interview and offered none of the things Abkhaz people would want to hear.

Inal Khashig: “From my strictly Abkhaz perspective, Gvaramia did not say anything radically new. If anything, he simply revived the old idea of resolving the Georgian-Abkhaz conflict through Georgia’s integration into the European Union, which would serve as an attractive incentive for Abkhaz people.

Georgian politicians have periodically put forward this idea since the presidency of Mikheil Saakashvili. The most recent was Georgia’s current prime minister, Irakli Kobakhidze, who in 2024 even set a specific deadline for achieving the goal. ‘Georgia will join the European Union together with our Abkhaz and Ossetian brothers by 2030,’ he declared at the time from a high-profile podium. In short, the EU idea has already been discussed many times.”

From Gvaramia’s interview, I also understood that Georgia cannot resolve the conflict through military means at present because it lacks the resources needed to guarantee the desired outcome. In this context, economic development and shared security interests should form the basis for resolving the conflict.

The only “new” idea proposed by the opposition politician is that Georgia needs to overcome the trauma it suffered after the Georgian-Abkhaz war of the 1990s because these memories “prevent it from moving forward and hold back development”. And on this point, I completely agree with Nika Gvaramia.

In my view, Georgia’s constant insistence on the need to regain Abkhazia is actually a heavy burden that prevents the country from achieving its full potential.

It is like a man who devotes all his energy and the rest of his life to trying to win back a wife who left him long ago. You can consider his life wasted.

I am convinced that if Mikheil Saakashvili had not abandoned his reform agenda in favour of “restoring territorial integrity” during his presidency, Georgia would almost certainly have made much greater progress in building its statehood.

I can well imagine that when Nika Gvaramia speaks about the need to overcome the trauma, he actually means giving up once and for all on claims to the lost territories. But as a politician, he understands the consequences of making such an admission openly.

As for the idea of restoring trust between Abkhaz people and Georgians, Gvaramia talks about this as well. But his understanding of “trust” is not very different from that of other Georgian politicians: essentially, “we will open up the world to you and shower you with benefits, but first come back to us”. In other words, it is a kind of bargain, with no guarantee that the other side is not bluffing.

But genuine trust looks very different.

In my view, a tangible step towards beginning the process of rebuilding trust between Abkhaz people and Georgians would be for Tbilisi to abolish the discriminatory Law on Occupied Territories, which does little short of preventing Abkhazia and South Ossetia from breathing freely without Georgia’s permission. But Nika Gvaramia did not mention this law even once. Perhaps that is why his interview went unnoticed in Abkhazia.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.



Nika Gvaramia interview

World.title: Opinion: ‘Removing Kobakhidze would be logical move for Ivanishvili if prime minister does not move against him first’
World.content:
Opinion on Georgian Prime Minister Kobakhidze

According to Eka Gigauri, executive director of Transparency International Georgia, removing Prime Minister Kobakhidze could eventually become a logical step for Ivanishvili — provided the prime minister does not manage to seize political power himself.

Eka Gigauri: “The Garibashvili case has once again confirmed what we already knew:”

None of this has anything to do with fighting corruption. Ivanishvili is reshuffling his inner circle, while Kobakhidze — with his approval and Mdinaradze’s assistance — is getting rid of political rivals. In “Georgian Dream”, no one is surprised when people enrich themselves at the public’s expense or engage in corruption: they all steal. The entire system is built on corruption, and Ivanishvili gave them the freedom to do so. So the “fight against corruption” is merely a staged performance designed to conceal a settling of scores. Kobakhidze does not get his hands dirty himself. He has Mdinaradze to do that for him, who has become his loyal executor and servant. It is obvious that the overwhelming majority of “Georgian Dream” supporters genuinely support Garibashvili. The same cannot be said of Kobakhidze and Mdinaradze. Look at the reactions from “Dream” supporters to statements by Garibashvili and his wife. If the authorities imprisoned Mdinaradze and then Kobakhidze, “Dream” supporters would not say a word in their defence. To them, Kobakhidze is still a former NGO worker and employee of international organisations. He is not a churchgoer and has no particular ties to the Church. The same applies to much of his team. There is no friendship, brotherhood or willingness to support one another in the “Georgian Dream” party. Apparently, none of them possesses that quintessential Georgian sense of honour. Out of fear of Bidzina, and now of Kobakhidze as well, they will betray one another, throw each other under the bus and abandon one another in times of trouble. Ivanishvili is deliberately deepening divisions within his own team and turning its members against one another. His goal is to prevent them from uniting against him and to force them to constantly undermine and confront each other. Today, Kobakhidze is clearly Ivanishvili’s favourite. However, he appears to have been carried away by this status. He often talks about his personal achievements, as though he had the power to act even without Ivanishvili. He may not have many genuine supporters within “Georgian Dream”, but today he exercises almost complete control over state institutions. “Georgian Dream” members appear to fear Kobakhidze greatly — perhaps even more than Bidzina. They know that Kobakhidze has direct access to Bidzina and can tell him something about a fellow party member that could ultimately destroy them. Even Garibashvili did not have this kind of influence. Kobakhidze has placed his people almost everywhere, while parliament is under his complete control. He has gradually concentrated enormous power in his hands. If this continues, even Ivanishvili may find it difficult to dismantle the system.

The experience of authoritarian regimes around the world also shows that dictators manage their inner circles according to the principle of “divide and rule”. They periodically replace their favourites and involve everyone in corruption schemes and other crimes, so that they can later use their weaknesses and complicity against them. At the same time, they pit influential groups against one another and keep everyone in a constant state of fear through selective punishment.

Thus, no individual or group can accumulate enough power to pose a real threat to the leader. However, such a system also carries a significant risk: a favourite who has concentrated all the levers of power in their hands may eventually begin building an independent political force. That is why dictators often get rid of their most loyal and influential allies.

At the same time, members of an authoritarian ruler’s inner circle often initiate changes of power. In other words, autocrats and dictators have good reason to fear their own inner circles. Today, if Kobakhidze wanted to, he could even remove Bidzina, and no one in “Georgian Dream” would dare oppose him. Therefore, removing Kobakhidze would eventually become a perfectly logical step — unless he managed to remove Ivanishvili first.

Opinion on Georgian Prime Minister Kobakhidze

World.title: President Ilham Aliyev send congratulatory letter to President of Kazakhstan
World.content:
Photo: Press service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 23. President Ilham Aliyev has sent a congratulatory letter to Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev on the successful holding of the first elections to the country's new parliament - the Kurultai.

This was reported by the press service of the President of Azerbaijan.

"Dear Kassym-Jomart Kemelevich,

I extend my sincerest congratulations to you and your brotherly people on the successful holding of the first elections to the new parliament of the Republic of Kazakhstan – Qurultay.

I express my confidence that this significant event, which marks the beginning of a new historical chapter in Kazakhstan’s socio-political life, will contribute to advancing your country’s comprehensive development, supporting the continuation of your large-scale reforms, and ensuring the successful implementation of the tasks ahead. I wish the Qurultay every success.

Advancing relations with Kazakhstan, with which we are closely bound by common roots, national-spiritual values, and brotherly ties, holds special importance for us. Our active and fruitful political dialogue has provided a strong impetus to further strengthening the Azerbaijan-Kazakhstan strategic partnership and enriching it with new substance.

I am confident that through our joint efforts, the friendly relations and strategic partnership between Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan, built on solid foundations, will continue to expand and deepen along an upward trajectory in line with the interests of our peoples.

Taking this opportunity, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations to you, wishing you robust health, happiness, and continued success in your high state activities, and to the brotherly people of Kazakhstan everlasting peace, progress, and prosperity," the letter reads.

World.title: Voting in Kazakhstan’s Kurultai elections concludes with 74.19% turnout
World.content:
ASTANA, Kazakhstan, August 23. Voting in Kazakhstan’s elections for deputies of the Kurultai has concluded, with voter turnout standing at 74.19% nationwide, Trend's special correspondent reports from Astana.

Polling stations across the country closed at 8:00 p.m. local time. According to the Central Election Commission (CEC), 9,352,151 voters had received ballots by 8:00 p.m., accounting for 74.19% of registered voters.

According to data provided by territorial election commissions of the capital, regions and cities of republican significance, voter turnout as of 8:00 p.m. was:

Astana – 51.67%

Abai Region – 81.41%

Akmola Region – 82.69%

Aktobe Region – 88.30%

Almaty Region – 71.17%

Atyrau Region – 70.74%

West Kazakhstan Region – 73.38%

Zhambyl Region – 85.18%

Zhetisu Region – 91.19%

Karaganda Region – 76.28%

Kostanay Region – 76.47%

Kyzylorda Region – 90.75%

Mangystau Region – 71.38%

Pavlodar Region – 71.20%

North Kazakhstan Region – 77.31%

Turkistan Region – 92.16%

Ulytau Region – 70.72%

East Kazakhstan Region – 87.50%

Almaty – 43.23%

Shymkent – 75.42%.

The CEC also reported that, as of 7:00 p.m. Astana time, all 79 polling stations at Kazakhstan’s diplomatic missions abroad had opened in 61 countries. Voting had already concluded in 11 countries by that time.

A total of 11,402 voters are registered at polling stations abroad. By the specified time, 6,007 people had voted.

Kazakhstan’s citizens in San Francisco, USA, will be the last to vote, with the polling station there having opened at 7:00 p.m. Astana time.

The elections to the Kurultai, Kazakhstan’s unicameral parliament envisaged by the new Constitution that entered into force on July 1, 2026, were held today.

The Kurultai will consist of 145 deputies elected for a five-year term. The elections are being held under a proportional representation system, with deputies elected from party lists in a single nationwide electoral district.

World.title: Zelenskyy rejects plea for wartime presidential election
World.content:
Holding a wartime election in Ukraine while active fighting with Russia continues would "destroy" the country by splitting Ukrainians, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

His comments, released to reporters on Sunday, were Mr Zelenskyy's first on the subject since ousted former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for a wartime poll in a bombshell address last week.

Mr Fedorov's surprise dismissal last month sparked widespread protests.

But supporters calling for his reinstatement later baulked at his call for an election, which is the first such demand by a major Ukrainian political figure since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

"I believe that if we want to destroy the country, then we can move towards elections during this kind of war," Mr Zelenskyy said.

Elections in war are prohibited by Ukrainian law. Analysts also say security concerns and the millions of Ukrainians abroad, under Russian occupation or fighting at the front mean it would be too difficult to hold an election.

Mykhailo Fedorov is calling for a presidential poll after being dumped as Ukraine's defence minister. (Reuters: Alina Smutko)

During the same address, Mr Zelenskyy disclosed figures showing Ukraine’s growing shortage of Patriot air defence missiles needed to counter Russian ballistic attacks, with deliveries from Western allies declining in the past three years, even as Russian missile strikes intensified.

He highlighted battlefield gains, however, saying Ukrainian forces have almost completely recaptured the Dnipropetrovsk region, with only about 10 square kilometres remaining under Russian control.

He made the remarks during a two-hour off-the-record meeting with reporters on Saturday, with a transcript released on Sunday.

Elections would split Ukraine, Zelenskyy warns

Mr Zelenskyy's approval rating has remained generally stable at about 60 per cent but pollsters have said that while Ukrainians want fresh faces in politics, many have little appetite for voting now.

Ukraine's drones could crash Russian banks On the outskirts of Russian cities, warehouses belonging to the country's largest online retailer are being struck by Kyiv's drones, with some analysts saying it could lead to a financial crisis.

An August 5 poll by the ​Kyiv International Institute of Sociology found that 57 per cent of Ukrainians want elections only after fighting ends.

Echoing his previous comments on the matter, Mr Zelenskyy said a wartime election might be possible if Kyiv's partners could guarantee security, but that no one has proposed such a plan.

"Elections right now are a tsunami for the state, which will split Ukraine," he said.

"That's why my strategy is to steer the country toward an ending of the war and to preserve an independent and sovereign state."

Mr Fedorov, a longtime Zelenskyy ally who has been seen as a top political challenger, did not explicitly say whether he would stand in any future election.

Reuters

World.title: Piastri struggles after slow pit stop, Norris wins as Verstappen crashes
World.content:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris has doubled his grand prix win tally in 2026, producing a pair of brilliant overtakes to win the Dutch Grand Prix.

Norris won the last grand prix in Hungary before the mid-year break, and continued that good form while teammate Oscar Piastri struggled for pace.

Mercedes championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who led for stretches in Zandvoort, finished second ahead of teammate George Russell who obeyed team orders in the late stages of the race.

Oscar Piastri was running third, but lost the position thanks to a slow pit stop. The Australian struggled for pace in the second half of the race and finished a distant sixth.

A slow pit stop from McLaren cost Oscar Piastri third place early in the Dutch Grand Prix. (Getty Images: LAP Images/Pauline Ballet)

But the day belonged to Norris, who lost the lead on a second restart after the race was red-flagged on the first lap after Max Verstappen lost control of his Red Bull and smashed into the barrier.

"A tough race. I made it tough for myself, but a good race, well fought," Norris said.

"Probably one of my better wins. We had to fight for it well, but the pace was very strong.

"I managed things incredibly well today. Over the moon, very, very happy and nice to win the final race here in Zandvoort."

Despite rain falling in the hour before the grand prix, all drivers started on dry tyres, but Verstappen lost control of his Red Bull on a damp part of the circuit and hit the barriers hard.

Norris lost the lead off the restart to Antonelli, with the teenager quicker in the opening laps.

Oscar Piastri, who lost a position at the race start, jumped from fifth into third at the restart and was in contention for a podium.

But the Australian suffered a slow pit stop on lap 18 of 72, dropping him behind Russell. Piastri would struggle for pace for the remainder of the grand prix.

As the race wore on, Norris proved to be quicker in his McLaren as Antonelli struggled with grip. The McLaren came in for his second stop seven laps later than Antonelli, giving him a massive tyre advantage.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was left out for much longer than his rivals, and was holding the lead of the race as Antonelli and Norris both caught him at the same time.

Norris produced a brilliant move around the outside of Antonelli into the first corner of lap 54, and then passed Hamilton later in the lap to re-take the lead and seal victory.

"The move [on Antonelli] was good, I knew I was not going to get many chances," Norris said.

"Every lap I spent behind him, my odds were getting lower and lower.

"I saw Lewis defending and I knew that was my moment.

"That move won me the race."

Some drivers, including Antonelli, pitted under a late virtual safety car. Antonelli dropped behind Russell, but Mercedes called team orders and the 19-year-old was allowed through.

Russell held on for third with Ferrari duo Hamilton and Charles Leclerc chasing him all the way to the finish line.

Liam Lawson, racing for Red Bull in place of the injured Isack Hadjar, placed seventh, ahead of Audi's Nico Hülkenberg.

With an upgraded car, Fernando Alonso was ninth for Aston Martin, while Pierre Gasly was 10th for Alpine.

Relive all the action of the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix on the blog below.

World.title: Iran president says nation has 'many problems' due to sanctions
World.content:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian admits his country's citizens face "many problems", after the United States launched a new wave of sanctions seeking to further isolate its economy.

"I understand we have many problems in society right now. We are trying to prevent these as much as we can," Mr Pezeshkian said in a speech broadcast on state television on Sunday.

His comments came after the US vowed last week to bring about the "collapse" of the Iranian regime through a newly announced sanctions campaign, nearly six months after the start of their war.

In his response, Mr Pezeshkian said that, because of US President Donald Trump, Iran was "in a full-scale economic, military and security war".

People at the Grand Bazaar in Tehran where prices are likely to rise due to sanctions. (Reuters: Majid Asgaripour/WANA)

"He says he is imposing the most crushing and terrifying sanctions on Iran," Mr Pezeshkian said.

The Iranian government has faced several waves of mass protest in recent years.

Iranians describe life under regime Three Iranians have shared their insights on life under the regime, as the war passes its fifth month.

They have often been triggered by economic hardships, including inflation and exchange rate swings, leading to declining purchasing power.

At the end of last year, a protest movement initially sparked by the rising cost of living turned into mass demonstrations denouncing those in power.

Authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths during the unrest, accusing the US and Israel of orchestrating the violence.

Foreign-based NGOs, however, said officials had launched an indiscriminate crackdown that left thousands dead.

Scott Bessent will go into detail about the new sanctions against Iran on Monday. (AP: Matt Rourke)

"We are striving with all our hearts to overcome inflation, livelihood problems, unemployment, and to secure the future of the people, so that they can live with dignity and pride," Mr Pezeshkian said on Sunday.

Since the war began on February 28, 3,636 people have reportedly died in Iran, with 2,100 estimated to be civilian deaths.

On Monday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will host a media conference to outline the exact details of the economic measures to be imposed on Iran.

AFP/ABC

World.title: Sydney shark attack victim reflects on 'second chance at life'
World.content:
Sydney shark attack victim Leah Stewart says she has not fully recovered more than two months after the incident, but feels like she has been given a "second chance at life".

Ms Stewart's family had previously provided updates on her condition on a fundraising site. On Sunday she wrote for the first time about her experience.

"After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I'm so happy that I've progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this," she said.

" I want you to know that I feel like I've been given a second chance at life, and I'm not going to waste it. "

Leah Stewart says the past few months have been "incredibly difficult". (Supplied: Stewart family)

On June 13, Ms Stewart was taken to St Vincent's Hospital in a critical condition after being mauled by a white shark while she was out for a morning swim, between the flags and close to the shore, at Coogee Beach in Sydney's east.

The 35-year-old was bitten on her leg and arms, suffered multiple fractures throughout her body and lost a lot of blood.

She was in an induced coma for days and underwent multiple surgeries, including the amputation of one of her arms.

'My recovery has been remarkable'

The mother-of-one said she has been focusing on her healing and doing everything in her "power to get back to some sort of normal life".

"I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable."

More than $500,000 has been raised to aid her recuperation, and while Ms Stewart profusely thanked the community for its generosity, she said it was time to "turn off donations".

"Because what you've offered has given us enough to recover, to stay in our home, and to give us options for further medical treatment down the road," she said.

Leah Stewart says the support she has received has "inspired me to get better, not bitter". (Supplied: Stewart family)

She added the support she had received locally and from all over the world had contributed to her recovery.

" You've inspired me to get better, not bitter. "

About 11 days after the attack, the 35-year-old teacher spoke to her family for the first time after she was briefly woken from an induced coma.

Her first words, at the time, to her husband and mother were "I love you".

"Her first thoughts were with her daughter, August, and wanted to check she was OK," Ms Stewart's brother said.

NSW has experienced a number of shark-related incidents this year.

In January, 12-year-old Nico Antic died in hospital after he was attacked at Vaucluse.

Later that month, musician Andre de Ruyter lost his leg after he was bitten by a suspected bull shark at Manly Beach.

The attacks have led to an expansion of a drone surveillance program, which now covers 72 beaches along the NSW coast from dawn to dusk.

World.title: Trump hits back at Canada after retaliatory tariffs announced
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has hit back at Canada after Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs on the United States following a breakdown in trade negotiations.

"Canada wants the benefits of being a State, without being one!!!" Mr Trump said in a post on Truth Social.

"They have also charged our great farmers, for many years, massive amounts of Tariffs. No more!!!" he said.

Since beginning his second term, Mr Trump has made numerous references to making Canada the "51st state" of America, which has infuriated the northern neighbours.

Earlier, Mr Carney said that new Canadian tariffs would take effect on September 8, notably targeting the US steel and dairy industries.

New 50 per cent US tariffs impacting about $US20 billion ($28 billion) worth of goods, or 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the US, came into force on Saturday.

Canadian and US steel products will be impacted by the tit-for-tat tariffs. (AP: Nick Iwanyshyn/The Canadian Press)

The "dollar for dollar" tariffs on imports of US steel, electronics and other products mark a further worsening of relations between the longtime allies and major trading partners.

The two countries failed to reach a trade deal late on Friday, with each side blaming the other for derailing three days of intensive negotiations.

The breakdown complicates the future of a US-Mexico-Canada free-trade pact.

Mr Trump's new tariffs hit sectors including wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing rods and hockey equipment,

These duties do not exempt Canadian products under the three-nation trade deal, which has shielded most Canadian exports to the US in the past 18 months.

A frosty relationship between Mark Carney (left) and Donald Trump (right) has hit a new low over tariffs. (AP: Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press, File)

The new US tariffs cover around 5 per cent of Canada's exports to the US.

They could expose some vulnerable industries such as softwood lumber and wine to severe damage and lead to job losses and business closures, trade experts have said.

PM says Trump considering tariff exemption Anthony Albanese says he has urged Donald Trump to consider giving Australia a full exemption from Washington's sweeping tariffs.

"We will be mobilising our network of businesses in all regions and all sectors to brace for impact and make the best of a bad situation," said Candace Laing, CEO of the Canadian Chamber of Commerce.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford, one of the most vocal opponents of US tariffs, supported Mr Carney's decision to retaliate.

"I'm glad he didn't sign that deal because it was a bad deal. It was a bad deal for Ontario. It was a bad deal for the auto sector, the steel sector, and the manufacturing sector," Mr Ford said.

There were also US proposals that affected Canadian culture, language and sovereignty, Mr Carney said, without elaborating.

He was elected last year on a promise to be a tough negotiator with Mr Trump, and remains broadly popular. Polls show most Canadians oppose making any concessions to the US.

"Canadians must stand united to defend our country against these unfair attacks on our jobs and businesses," Pierre Poilievre, the leader of the official opposition Conservative Party, said in a statement.

Wires/ABC

World.title: Immersive experiences at heart of Powerhouse Parramatta grand opening
World.content:
A crystal tunnel set within a meteorite, a maze of mirrors and a vintage Qantas plane will be among the exhibits on offer when Powerhouse Parramatta opens its doors on November 7.

The full program for the museum's grand opening was revealed on Sunday, with work continuing to install more than 3,000 objects sourced from Australia and around the world.

The museum is promising an immersive experience, including an exhibition of five major works by British artist Es Devlin.

The Turning includes a labyrinth of mirrors called the Forest of Us.

The Forest of Us artwork involves a labyrinth of mirrors. (Supplied: Andrea Mora)

Visitors will be encouraged to get lost in its light-filled maze, while discovering the "striking visual symmetries" between trees and human lungs.

Powerhouse CEO Lisa Havilah said one of the "beautiful things" about the new space at Parramatta was its flexibility, allowing for large-scale installations.

"We're able to create these exhibitions that people will really be able to immerse themselves in," Ms Havilah said.

" It's also about presenting the collection in new ways as well. "

Devlin's Memory Palace will also feature in the exhibition. (Supplied: Powerhouse Parramatta)

Devlin's other works include Memory Palace, an immersive 3D cityscape, and Collective Portrait, which will invite visitors to draw portraits of strangers.

'Don't be scared' of the dark

An immersive experience catering to children will be an exhibition called The Dark.

"The Dark can be wondrous. There's no need to be scared," the museum's program teases.

The Dark is among the exhibitions catering to children. (Supplied: Powerhouse Parramatta)

Ms Havilah said the exhibition would be set inside a meteorite-like installation, showcasing more than 800 objects including an impressive minerals collection.

"There's a crystal tunnel, there are objects that make noise.

"There are different perspectives of how you imagine the dark, whether it's deep into space, deep underwater or deep in your body."

The Dark will also display the cherished personal objects of children from across Western Sydney.

"We did a call-out and 100 kids … have loaned us their most special object," Ms Havilah said.

"So there's a whole room with these 100 objects, but also the stories behind each of [them]."

One room will feature the favourite objects from 100 children across Western Sydney. (Supplied: Powerhouse Parramatta)

Walking on water

The third of the new exhibitions announced is a First Nations-led work called Overflow.

Through the films of acclaimed director and Kamilaroi man Ivan Sen, visitors can learn about Aboriginal custodianship of the oceans, rivers and other waterways in NSW.

According to the Powerhouse, Overflow will shine a light on cultural practices that foster species protection, flood mitigation, sustainable and commercial fishing and water quality.

Films by Kamilaroi man Ivan Sen are part of the Overflow exhibition. (Supplied: Powerhouse Parramatta )

Ms Havilah said audiences would be invited to "walk on water" as part of the exhibition.

"There will be a huge platform in the middle of the space that will have water in the middle of it," she said.

There will be five opening exhibitions, two of which were previously announced.

Task Eternal will explore the "human ambition to defy gravity", and the display will include a NASA moon rock and original drawings of flying machines by Leonardo da Vinci.

It will also feature the Avro 504K— a replica of the very first Qantas plane.

A replica of the very first Qantas plane will be on display when the museum opens. (Supplied: Powerhouse Parramatta )

Another exhibition, The Mall, will span two storeys of the Powerhouse, exploring the history and evolution of the modern shopping centre.

Western Sydney will get another nod in this exhibition, as the birthplace of the Westfield shopping centre — a concept that was exported to the world.

Rare items from Australian fashion brands will be on show, along with the signature jeans worn by Apple co-founder Steve Jobs.

The display will also include prototypes of the Predator boot, conceived by Australian footballer Craig Johnston and worn by David Beckham.

The Mall will be exhibited over two storeys of the museum. (Supplied: Jo Duck)

Kids see it for free

All of the exhibitions will be free of charge for visitors under 16 years of age.

However, Task Eternal will attract an as-yet undisclosed entry fee for visitors who are 16 years old and over.

Powerhouse Parramatta opening date revealed The NSW government announced in May that construction of the $915 million museum had been completed four years after work began.

Ms Havilah said the museum was designed to increase Sydneysiders' access to "world-class arts and culture."

"It's a really great gift," she said.

"To have four of the five exhibitions free to the public, I think is incredible."

Arts Minister John Graham said the $915 million project, which also includes storage and archiving, would offer good value to families facing cost-of-living pressures.

"We want to ensure that price isn't a barrier for young people to explore the big ideas, the creativity, the innovation that Powerhouse Parramatta will exhibit and celebrate," he said.

World.title: Quick hits: A Shoriful stunner amid more left-arm carnage in the 29th two-day Test
World.content:
Mitchell Starc delivers once more but it's another left-arm seamer who delivers the ball of the series, as Test cricket is blessed with its 29th two-day match.

Here are the quick hits from day two of the second Test between Australia and Bangladesh.

1. Shoriful's ball of the series

Cameron Green was felled by a brutal inswinging yorker. (Getty Images: Cricket Australia/Albert Perez)

It wouldn't have taken a rocket scientist to determine that Cam Green held the key for Australia at the start of day two.

The towering all-rounder, buoyed by his drought-breaking ton in Darwin, was once again looking precisely the player he had for so long promised to be.

With Green well set on 67 and clattering boundaries to either side of the wicket, it was going to take something special to remove the big man.

And Shoriful Islam, having already ripped through Australia's middle order late on day two, delivered something very, very special.

The left-armer's pinpoint yorker swung in late and dramatically, with Green falling over himself in a futile attempt to keep it out.

The ball thudded into the Australian's big toe on its way past the stumps and, after a brief consultation with DRS, was given out LBW to what was surely the ball of the series.

And that wasn't the end of the story for left-arm seamers on day two …

2. Starc continues the left-arm carnage

Mitchell Starc picked up from where he left off in the second innings. (Getty Images: Albert Perez/Cricket Australia)

Shoriful, who was almost inconceivably yanked from the bowling attack after that stunner against Green, ended the innings with figures of 7-48, the best-ever return for a Bangladeshi bowler while playing away from home.

Combine that with the 6-12 Mitchell Starc plundered early on day one, and left-arm seam had returned overall figures of 13-60, while accounting for 13 of the 20 wickets to fall in the match.

And it wasn't long before those numbers were improved even further.

He couldn't manage a wicket in his first set, but Starc struck with his eighth delivery of the innings, extracting some extra bounce to have Shadman Islam caught off a leading edge at point.

And the very next ball, Starc had his eighth of the match, having kissed the top of Mominul Haque's off stump with the Bangladeshi attempting an ill-advised leave.

An almost-customary double strike from Australia's supreme new-ball destroyer.

Starc eventually finished with figures of 4-39 for the innings and, with 10-51, the second-best match figures of his career.

3. Smith takes a screamer after tea

Tailender Taskin Ahmed had set himself well in the lead-up to the tea break, but he fell at the very first hurdle in the evening session.

Lyon's first delivery was a beauty, pitching and turning away from the leftie, who swung hard and found a healthy outside edge.

And Steve Smith, in place at his familiar position at slip, had to have his wits about him to complete a very good one-handed grab.

He's Test cricket's most prolific catcher for a reason, after all.

Taskin, who had provided perhaps Bangladesh's brightest spot in an otherwise pitch-black innings in swatting a massive six over long on in the shadows of tea, was out for 7.

4. The shortest session ever?

With Shoriful in at No. 11, the end was very clearly nigh in Mackay.

However, Shoriful showed in the first innings that he had at least some ability with the bat, top scoring with a rather frenetic 14 from 19 deliveries.

He survived the first ball of his second dig, defending Lyon out into the off side.

But it was all over with the very next ball.

Shoriful had a big swing at one, caught a thick outside edge and ballooned a dolly out to Starc at point, with Australia's superlative spearhead fittingly bringing the match to an end.

With two wickets falling in just three balls, it had to be close to the shortest non-weather-affected session in Test history.

5. The 29th two-day Test

Australia cruised to victory within two days. (Getty Images: Albert Perez/Cricket Australia)

There have been 2,632 Test matches played in cricket's lengthy red-ball history, with 457 of them held in Australia.

As of today, there have been just 29 finish inside two days.

Only five of those have happened in Australia.

And yet, in the last 20 Tests that have been played on these shores, it has happened four times.

Australia thumped South Africa on a Gabba green top in 2022, and then there were two, two-day Tests during last summer's Ashes, one in Perth and the other at the MCG.

The only Australia-hosted Test to finish inside two days before that game in Brisbane four years ago took place in Melbourne against the West Indies, in February 1931.

Eleven of the two-day Tests in history took place before World War I (between 1882 and 1912), a further three either side of World War II (1931-1946) but then none between 1946 and 1999.

Then, since 2000, there have been 13 two-day Tests. The cost of a fast-paced world, perhaps.

World.title: Swans AFLW captain says support 'just unbelievable' as record smashed
World.content:
Sydney AFLW captain Lucy McEvoy wasn't sure what to expect for her side when they ran out for the first instalment of a historic double-header at the SCG.

The Swans dominated headlines across the country all week, filling both front and back pages of every newspaper, for a scandal that called the club's culture into question.

Swans fans descend on SCG amid club scandal Sydney Swans fans react to an emotional week, where a scandal continues to engulf the club, as they prepare to watch a historic double header at the SCG.

What the women's team got was an outpouring of support which broke the side's attendance record with 16,672 fans filling the stands to watch them play.

That is more than double the previous club record of 8,264.

"It's amazing. We weren't sure what we were going to expect this week, but to see the support that we've received today is just unbelievable," McEvoy told Fox Footy after the game.

"The members and fans are so tight and they know that we're united as a club and we're better than what we were at the start of the week.

The Swans doubled its crowd attendance record. (Getty: Cameron Spencer)

"I'm just so grateful to have the support that we had today and the girls were able to turn it on.

"We had a few nervous girls, that's for sure, but we absolutely turned it on."

The scenes were particularly celebratory on the ground post-siren, after Sydney beat Essendon by 24 points.

It was just the second time the women have played on the SCG for premiership points and the first in a double billing with the men's.

Loading Instagram content

Before locking in to warm up, star men's players Errol Gulden and captain Callum Mills got around the women's players.

Gulden was also seen going up to the crowd giving the fans a big thank you for turning out in droves.

Some of those fans left before the men's game, as a boycott had been suggested in the days before the match as a scandal continues to engulf the club.

It's unclear how many fans left in protest to the scandal, but a steady stream was seen leaving.

Swans players spent time with fans after the game. (Getty: Cameron Spencer)

Five players — Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon — have been stood down by the Swans for breaching the club's standards on drinking and staying out late following last Sunday's win over Essendon in Melbourne.

Police from Victoria's sexual crimes squad are separately investigating a report of sexual assault, which the ABC understands centres on a player allegedly touching a woman without her consent.

Police have not made any arrests or laid charges.

Swans fans cheer from the stands. (Getty: Darrian Traynor/AFL Photos)

Lulu Clarke, who has been a Sydney Swans fan for as long as she can remember, was one of the fans who walked out.

Ms Clarke had bought a ticket to the men's game, unaware the women were also playing, but once the news broke of the incident she knew she would not be staying for both games.

"Of late, I've definitely drifted apart from the Swans and the AFL industry as a whole," Ms Clarke said.

"I decided that I'm absolutely not going to the men's game, even if those five players were still stood down. There's no way I could just show up and watch it. It just didn't sit right with me."

Former Matilda Sarah Walsh also left the stadium after the women's game, saying it had been a "tough week", but stressed she was not boycotting the men's team.

"It's not a new story but I have a five-year-old daughter who I brought here today to support the women's team," Ms Walsh said.

"I think you can have a club and not expect someone to be a fan of both teams.

"I think that's the nuance of sport, don't expect Socceroos fans to be Matildas fans … We've got a long way to go in society. I don't think this is a Sydney Swans issue at all … it's a societal issue and we all need to do better."

Swans fans Kayley and Georgia went to the SCG to support the AFLW side. (ABC)

Swans fans Kayley and Georgia told ABC News they were there to support the women and will likely just watch a bit of the men's game.

"It's very disappointing from the men's team … I feel like we were very disappointed in everything that happened," Georgia said.

Kayley said the situation was upsetting.

"We've been supporting the Swans since we were kids as well. So, it was just shocking," she said.

"We never thought that any players from this team could do something like this. It was really upsetting."

Many fans held signs during the game along the lines of "I'm here for AFLW".

World.title: Dutch F1 Grand Prix live: Norris wins final Zandvoort race after Verstappen’s horror smash, Piastri’s day of frustration
World.content:
Here’s what the top three said to Sky Sports after the Dutch Grand Prix...

Lando Norris speaks after winning the Dutch Grand Prix. Getty Images

Lando Norris (1st): “[That was an] amazing, amazing – a tough race. Yesterday I said we need to put on a bit of a show for everyone for the final race here … it’s probably one of my better wins. We had to fight for it well, but the pace was very strong ... I’m over the moon, very, very happy and it’s nice to win the final race here in Zandvoort.

“The move [the race-winning overtake on Antonelli] was good – I knew I wasn’t going to get many chances, every lap I spent behind them my odds were getting lower and lower.

“I saw Lewis defended, and I knew that was my moment. I did a couple clicks of brake balance, I knew I was going to commit to the braking and that move won me the race. Just well played from my part. I knew I had to make it.

“I probably had one chance to make it happen and I made the most of it. Another win here, very happy.”

Kimi Antonelli (2nd): ”It was a very intense race.

“[I] managed to get the lead and stint one I felt actually OK, but from stint two onwards just didn’t have the feeling with the car.

“I was sliding a lot with the car and at the end Lando passed me and I knew I had no chance after that.

“But then, of course, George was a great team player and [I’m] really happy for him to hold on to P3 as well.”

George Russell (3rd): “It was a difficult start for me, obviously losing the position [to Antonelli].

“These two [Norris and Antonelli] were very quick at the beginning, [and] then Lando was exceptionally fast towards the end of the race.

“It was tough to hold on on those old tyres. [I’m] happy to be standing here on the podium because it could have gone either way.

“Kimi was ahead of me anyway [before team orders came], so he deserved to finish ahead. Of course when you’re in the race, you want to fight for every single position.”

World.title: Why $130,000 a year is no longer enough to avoid housing stress in WA
World.content:
PropertyNewsRenting Why $130,000 a year is no longer enough to avoid housing stress in WA Cameron Myles August 24, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A yearly salary of $130,000 is still not enough to safeguard against rising rents in Western Australia, new research reveals. The state’s north has emerged as the nation’s most expensive region to rent in, according to the latest Priced Out report from affordable housing coalition Everybody’s Home. The report, released on Monday, shines a light on the sharp rise in rental prices in recent years, and measures how much of a person’s weekly income is spent on rent, based on median weekly prices. It set out that no more than 30 per cent of a household budget should be allocated to rents to avoid financial stress.



Perth renters on low incomes would spend as much as 97 per cent of their weekly wage on the median asking rent for a unit (in the case of someone earning $40,000 a year). Related Article WA residential property This WA mining town is one of Australia’s fastest-growing property markets Even someone earning $130,000 a year and living in Perth would spend 36 per cent of their income on housing, “demonstrating that Perth remains unaffordable even for many higher-income households”. In the Pilbara and Kimberley – jointly referred to as “northern WA” – median rents exceed the disposable income of people earning $40,000-$50,000 a year, and is 99 per cent of the income of someone earning $60,000 a year. “While Perth remains one of the country’s least affordable capital cities, some regional markets are even more expensive relative to local incomes,” the report states.



In Busselton, Sharon, who asked her last name not be used, knows all too well the pressures of rising rents. At 55 years old, she would prefer to live alone. But, with her rent at $700 a week, and her Centrelink medical support income only providing about $515 a week, she is forced to sublet her home, which brings its own challenges. “It’s only affordable for me because I’m sharing with two other people,” Sharon said. “I desperately would love to live in my own place where I look after me, and I look after my dog. “Some [housemates] just don’t get it, and then when they no longer want to live here, they just pack up and leave.



“I’m left with the rent to pay on the room if nobody else is in there immediately. “And then I’m left with welcoming new strangers into my life and into my home.” Even with housemates, Sharon is still paying about $240 on rent. She gets by with the help of SecondBite, operated through the St Mary’s Church Family Centre, and leftover stock from a local baker, which she also gives to the Salvation Army. “If I didn’t have those two free food outlets, I would struggle, I would seriously struggle,” she said. Everybody’s Home spokesperson Maiy Azize said regional Australia was no longer a rental refuge and, in some areas, rents were now pricier than in the capital cities.



“Workers are losing weeks worth of their time and pay cheques to fund rent rises,” she said. Related Article Exclusive

Schools How Perth’s most in-demand schools impact nearby property prices “National rents are almost $50 extra a week compared to 18 months ago. “For someone earning $40,000, this rent increase would chew up nearly four and a half weeks worth of their working year. “For most workers, that’s more time than they get off all year.”



Azize laid the blame at the feet of “decades of governments” walking away from public and community housing. “These are the homes that don’t price out renters, and they’re the homes that private developers won’t build,” she said. “The federal government needs to build public and community homes at scale. Australia needs nearly one million of these homes within the next 15 years. “The federal government has shown that it can take action to help people buy their first home, now it must help everyone afford to rent one.” Sharon, however, believed councils had a lot to answer for – especially in Busselton, a popular tourist town that is awash with short-term holiday accommodation like Airbnb.



There are eight Airbnb properties on her block alone, and about 20 in the broader area within 200 metres of her house. She understands the appeal of the market, and even worked in the short-term accommodation sector when she was in Port Douglas, in Queensland, before moving back to the seaside town she grew up in. “Airbnb’s have created the housing crisis that we are facing now in 2026,” she said. “Immigration hasn’t changed, and the places that those people get placed in hasn’t changed. “Since people recovered from COVID and people started travelling again, I believe that’s when the Airbnb’s just went out of control.”



The City of Busselton has recently moved to tamp down the short-term accommodation market, banning unhosted holiday homes in some areas of the South West town. The town, on the coast of Geographe Bay in WA’s South West, had seen a strong population increase over the past two decades, even at one point being the fastest-growing local government area in the state. According to the Priced Out report, a renter on $40,000 a year in the South West would spend about 76 per cent of their income on rent, with the “affordability” benchmark of 30 per cent of weekly earnings only being met by those on incomes of $120,000 and above. “The Wheatbelt, Mid and South West are more affordable than Perth, although households on low and middle incomes continue to experience rental stress,” the report notes.

World.title: Labor’s plan to reserve more domestic gas stirs hopes of a revival
World.content:
BusinessCompaniesEnergy Labor’s plan to reserve more domestic gas stirs hopes of a revival Nick Toscano August 24, 2026 — 12:00am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Australia’s push to reserve more gas for domestic customers is stirring hopes of an onshore industrial revival, as a major chemical firm weighs reactivating a production complex mothballed nearly a decade ago due to surging gas prices. From next July, landmark regulations will compel shippers of eastern Australian liquefied natural gas to divert the equivalent of up to 20 per cent of their export volumes to local homes and businesses. Coogee Chemicals team leader Sergio Uliana, process engineer Mindy Zhu and production manager Vithal Ravavarapu at the mothballed chemical plant in Laverton. Eddie Jim The policy aims to undo the fallout from the mid-2010s, when a boom in LNG exports from Queensland exposed local gas users to global prices and made it increasingly difficult for gas-intensive manufacturers to secure affordable supplies of the fuel. A shuttered petrochemical facility in Melbourne’s west is positioned to be among the first beneficiaries of the federal policy shift. Coogee Chemicals placed its Laverton methanol plant on care and maintenance in 2016, eliminating 38 jobs, after its gas costs soared from $3 to more than $8 a gigajoule, and it was unable to secure a long-term supply deal, making its operations unviable.



Produced primarily from natural gas, methanol is a widely used chemical that is converted into formaldehyde, a building block for resins and adhesives in engineered wood, building materials and coatings. “For methanol, gas is the No.1 cost,” Coogee chief executive Grant Lukey said. ‘The reservation policy … could create a renaissance in the manufacturing sector.’ Coogee chief executive Grant Lukey Gas prices rose sharply along the eastern seaboard from 2015 as three giant LNG terminals on Queensland’s Curtis Island began cooling gas down to a liquid and shipping it overseas. The projects linked the domestic market to global LNG prices for the first time, just as Australia’s cheap legacy gas fields in the Bass Strait were also rapidly depleting. This sent costs sharply higher for households that used gas for cooking, heating and hot water, and put further pressure on manufacturers that relied on gas to fire their kilns and furnaces or as a feedstock for chemicals, plastic and fertiliser.



Coogee was among the first manufacturers to shut down a site, saying high gas prices and a scarcity of affordable long-term supply offers had pushed the facility to the wall. The federal government has resisted setting a specific gas price reduction under the reservation scheme, but it says the policy will create an oversupply in the domestic market that would place “downward pressure” on prices. Matt Flugge, chief executive of industry body Chemicals Australia, said gas below $10 a gigajoule, delivered on long-term contracts, was critical to support an “investible future” for chemicals manufacturing. He described the potential restart of Coogee Chemicals’ methanol plant as a case study of what an effective domestic gas policy could deliver, including the return of manufacturing jobs and the rebuilding of critical manufacturing capability. “Getting the gas reservation scheme design right will unlock new Australian chemicals manufacturing investment and value-add Australian gas to create products for Australian business and consumers,” Flugge said. Building product maker Borg, which employs 3500 people at its manufacturing sites nationally, has had to import methanol since the mothballing of Coogee’s Laverton plant in 2016. “Having a guaranteed supply of methanol is essential to our timber production lines and supports up to 2500 direct jobs in our facilities,” a spokesperson for Woodchem, a Borg company, said. However, the government’s push to force a significant volume of additional gas into the domestic market is setting up a fierce showdown with industry leaders and some major producers in the energy sector. Oil and gas companies say deliberately creating a market oversupply will artificially depress prices, making investment in new gas fields uneconomic and ultimately raising the risk of future supply shortages and price shocks.



In a recent analysis prepared for the gas industry, research firm Wood Mackenzie found gas accounted for less than 5 per cent of the combined operating costs of the 13 industrial facilities in eastern Australia that consume the most gas. Reducing wholesale gas prices from $12 to $10 a gigajoule would lower those plants’ combined annual operating costs by just $94 million while lifting average profit margins by 0.4 per cent, it said. Related Article Energy Gas giants to reap $18 billion war windfall, reviving export tax calls The report also found that many of Australia’s largest manufacturers had long-term gas supply contracts to 2035 and beyond, meaning any changes to wholesale gas prices would have minimal or no impact on current operations. Australian Energy Producers, which represents oil and gas companies, said the findings reinforced concerns that the government’s proposed reservation framework would undermine investment in new gas supply while delivering only marginal benefits for manufacturers. “Cheaper gas is not the panacea for the competitiveness challenges facing Australian manufacturing,” Australian Energy Producers chief Samantha McCulloch said. World.title: Swans’ AFLW team ride support for win; Magpies battling; Carlton on song
World.content:
With a record crowd behind them, Sydney’s AFLW team have put the club’s AFL team’s hotel scandal aside to claim a 24-point win over Essendon at the SCG.

On Thursday, five AFL players - Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon - were suspended for the rest of the season for “breaching club standards”.

Swans players celebrate a goal in their win over Essendon. Getty Images

Separately, a police investigation continues into an alleged sexual assault at East Melbourne’s Pullman Hotel in the early hours of Monday morning.

Then, on Friday, AFLW captain Lucy McEvoy urged Sydney fans to stick with the club.

But with a record crowd of 16,672 fans behind them, the Colin O’Riordan-coached Swans scored a 9.12 (66) to 6.6 (42) victory that took them to a 2-0 record.

Sydney players gather after the AFLW victory on Sunday. Getty Images

“It’s amazing,” McEvoy told Fox Footy.

“We weren’t sure what we were going to be expecting this week, but to see the support that we’ve received today is just unbelievable.

“Our members and fans are so tight, and they know that we’re united as a club, and we’re better than what we were at the start of the week.

“And I’m just so grateful to have the support that we do today, and the girls were able to turn it on for them, so it was really good.”

Sofia Hurley greets fans after the Swans win over Essendon. Getty Images

The announcement of the crowd - more than double the Swans’ previous record - was met with a huge roar and delighted the players.

“Even when we ran out to start the game through the banner, it was just absolutely unbelievable,” McEvoy said.

“We had a few nervous girls, that’s for sure, but we absolutely turned it on.”

Laura Gardiner (31 disposals, six clearances and a goal) was huge, along with Sofia Hurley (23 disposals, 10 tackles, one goal) and Ally Morphett (30 hitouts, eight clearances, 18 disposals).

Swans AFLW fans had plenty to cheer about at the SCG. Getty Images

Taylor Smith kicked two goals while Zippy Fish (23 disposals, nine intercepts) and McEvoy were strong.

Essendon’s Maddison Prespakis (32 disposals) was immense with help from Amy Gaylor (22 disposals), Georgia Nanscawen (13 contested possessions) and Sophie Alexander (three goals).

Sydney were wasteful early, and Bonnie Toogood snapped the Bombers out to a game-high nine-point lead in the third quarter.

But then the Swans exploded to life.

Superstar Chloe Molloy put the Swans back in front - celebrating her goal with a ‘W’ sign with her hands - and Sydney never looked back, kicking away.

The Swans never looked back.

AAP

World.title: Dogs vs Pies to launch wildcards on Friday; Hawks lock down first AFL double chance since 2018
World.content:
Breaking SportAFLAFL 2026 Dogs vs Pies to launch wildcards on Friday; Hawks lock down first AFL double chance since 2018 Peter Ryan and Scott Spits Updated August 23, 2026 — 10:31pm ,first published 1:51pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Loading

A Western Bulldogs-Collingwood showdown on Friday night and Melbourne to take on Carlton the following night will feature in the AFL’s inaugural wildcard weekend. The Bulldogs’ upset win over the Demons on Saturday and Adelaide’s thumping of the Giants later that night confirmed the match-ups. Carlton captain Patrick Cripps has guided his team into the wildcard finals. Getty Images The AFL waited to announce which match will be played in each timeslot until after Hawthorn’s big win against West Coast at Optus Stadium on Sunday night. That is relevant to the wildcard fixture because the team that finishes fifth will play the ladder’s lowest advancing team, while sixth will play the higher-ranked team of the winners.



View post on X THE MATCH-UPS Friday, 28th August: Wildcard Final - Western Bulldogs v Collingwood. MCG, 7.40pm AEST

Wildcard Final - Western Bulldogs v Collingwood. MCG, 7.40pm AEST Saturday, 29th August: Wildcard Final - Melbourne v Carlton. MCG, 7.35pm AEST Hawthorn’s win tonight mean the Hawks finish fourth with the Cats fifth and Adelaide sixth. Because all wildcard teams are Victorian, the likely outcome of a Hawks win on Sunday night would mean one team would have to travel to Adelaide – which caused the delay in the league’s wildcard announcement as it works through potential fixturing for the next week of the finals series. All eyes on Collingwood: Bulldog Marcus Bontempelli. Getty Images



Watson takes jaw-dropping mark as Hawks crush Eagles Jack Gunston kicked five goals in his 300-game milestone and Nick Watson took a spectacular mark of the year contender as Hawthorn’s bid to snare third spot fell just short in a 62-point win over West Coast in Perth. Hawthorn entered Sunday night’s match needing to win in the vicinity of 90-100 points to leapfrog Brisbane into third spot. That would have meant the Hawks (15-6-2) would face the decimated Swans in Sydney in the first qualifying final instead of minor premiers Fremantle in Perth. Things were looking good for Hawthorn when they skipped out to an 83-25 lead midway through the third quarter following Watson’s moment of magic.



View post on X Aptly nicknamed The Wizard, Watson leapt onto the shoulders of Liam Baker and pushed off powerfully with his legs to take a spectacular midair mark before crashing to the turf. In the immediate aftermath, Baker and Watson smiled at each other in disbelief as they soaked up the moment, with Watson giving his opponent a hug after nailing the shot. But the wet and slippery conditions meant Hawthorn always faced an uphill battle to push the margin towards triple figures, with the Hawks forced to eventually settle for a 16.11 (107) to 6.9 (45) win in front of 43,066 fans at Optus Stadium. Hawthorn still finished fourth, earning a finals double chance for the first time since 2018.

World.title: Swans crisis deepens as fresh allegations of ‘multiple sexual assaults’ emerge
World.content:
At least one fresh allegation of sexual assault and multiple claims of sexual conduct without consent have been made by the three women at the centre of an investigation involving Sydney Swans players at the Pullman East Melbourne. They come as police were alerted to the potential existence of a recording relating to the events at the hotel in the early hours of last Monday. The Pullman hotel in East Melbourne, where the Sydney Swans players stayed. Simon Schluter The new allegation from the woman represented by Jackson Pannam of Slater & Gordon, is that she was the victim of “multiple sexual assaults”. Allegations against multiple men



The other two women are being represented by firm Carbone Lawyers. Multiple sources close to those women with knowledge of the matter, but not authorised to speak publicly, told this masthead they had alleged to police that they were subjected to conduct of a sexual nature beyond what was agreed to with multiple men when they were engaged as topless waitresses. The statements will form part of the police investigations into potential criminal conduct. The three women were engaged for the players and their friends during a night of partying following the team’s victory over Essendon at the MCG in round 23. Slater & Gordon said the sexual assaults alleged by its client were reported to Victoria Police, who have maintained to date they are investigating “a report of a sexual assault”. When asked specifically by this masthead on Sunday whether the investigation was broadened to include two of the women’s separate allegations of sexual conduct without consent, a Victoria Police spokesperson said, “we have nothing further to add”. This masthead is not suggesting that any of the men in the room engaged in conduct of a sexual nature without consent, only that it has been alleged.



“We are not providing ongoing commentary around this investigation,” a police spokeswoman said. A reported recording Two AFL industry sources, who wished to remain anonymous, confirmed that the Swans passed details of the potential recording to the police via the AFL after a person contacted the club claiming to have information that could be relevant to the investigation. This masthead does not claim to know whether the recording exists or what information it may contain, only that a person contacted the club about its existence before their details were referred to police. Swans players (from left) Chad Warner, James Jordon, Isaac Heeney, Riley Bice and Nick Blakey have been suspended for the rest of the season. Artwork: Marija Ercegovac



The Swans have confirmed five of their players – Issac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon – were in the hotel room in the early hours of August 17. The players have been banned by their club for breaching its behavioural standards, for which they apologised. But a source with knowledge of the situation has previously told this masthead that the players deny any criminal wrongdoing. Other men, including recently retired Swans player Taylor Adams, were also in the room. Adams has not responded to requests for comment by this masthead. It is not clear which men the allegations are about. The AFL integrity unit steps back from making inquiries about such matters to let the police investigation run its course. Police have not yet interviewed the five suspended players. Each of the women last week made statements to Victoria Police outlining their version of events. Victoria Police on Saturday confirmed its investigation was continuing.



Related Article Updated

AFL 2026 ‘No culture is perfect’: Swans launch a review into late-night party that rocked the club “Detectives from the sexual crimes squad continue to investigate a report of a sexual assault in East Melbourne on 17 August,” a police statement read. “The exact circumstances of the matter are still being established and a number of people have been spoken to.” The police investigation Carbone Lawyers said on Friday that it was preparing to launch legal action in the Supreme Court of Victoria against the five players and the club.



The lawyer representing the two women who alleged sexual conduct without consent told this masthead that the legal proceedings would be launched in the Common Law Division of the Victorian Supreme Court, with the women set to claim damages for pain and suffering, psychological injury and economic loss. Related Article Opinion

Gender equality From the Swans to Scots: Blaming the alleged victim means a harrowing truth can be avoided Jacqueline Maley Columnist and senior journalist “We are currently investigating the circumstances and preparing to commence legal proceedings against the club and potentially the individuals involved,” Manny Carbone, a partner at Carbone Lawyers, said. “Our clients are extremely traumatised and feel that their dignity and personal rights have been seriously violated by the events of Monday.” The Swans have denied there were any other club officials or staff members in the hotel room.



This masthead has previously reported that two sources familiar with the police investigation, but not authorised to speak publicly, confirmed drugs were involved in the early morning incident. However, both said the Swans teammates had denied being responsible for the drugs being there or taking them.
